Los resultados mostraron una reducción del 37 % en el tiempo de entrega, pasando de 67 a 42 días, y un incremento del 60 % en la capacidad de producción; además, el análisis financiero indicó una Tasa Interna de Retorno (IRR) del 30,24 %. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Planificar, Hacer, Verificar, Actuar) radica en la evidencia de que la aplicación de Lean Six Sigma permite ajustes cuantificables en la fase de “Hacer” y “Verificar”, facilitando la monitorización continua y la sostenibilidad de las mejoras a largo plazo.

articulos.titulo: A Lean-Based Integrated Production Model Combining Layout Optimization and Visual Control for Metalworking SMEs
articulos.revista: International Journal of Recent Engineering Science
articulos.resumen_en: Metalworking SMEs in developing economies had suffered inefficiencies for a long time, even after Lean and layout adjacent studies that reported only partial gains. This initiative addressed urgent issues of variability, huge amounts of internal transport, weak standardization of work processes, and unreliable production information. An integrated production model based on Lean Manufacturing, Systematic Layout Planning, and Kanban-type visual control was proposed and tested out in a Peruvian metalworking SME. New work methods were designed, plant layout was optimized, and information flow was improved with simple means of visual records. Results indicated that production efficiency improved from 80.20% to 90.80%, that systemic time per product was reduced by 9.44%, total travel time also by 8.13%, while information recording errors were reduced by 60.34%. Results indicated that some degree of operational stability was attained with measurable improvements in productivity, all without expending large amounts of capital. Theoretically, the initiative added more empirical information about synchronizing methods, spaces, and information in SMEs. From a social point of view, it is hoped that the additional competitiveness thus gained will contribute to reliable delivery ability extending downstream. Further studies are desired to extend the model.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio fue diseñar e implementar un modelo de producción integrado basado en Lean Manufacturing, Systematic Layout Planning (SLP) y Kanban visual para mejorar la eficiencia de una pequeña y mediana empresa (SME) de trabajo de metales en Perú. El contexto se centra en la industria metalúrgica peruana, donde las empresas enfrentan variabilidad, transporte interno excesivo y falta de estandarización de procesos. El método combinó la planificación sistemática de layout (SLP) con la creación de nuevas normas de trabajo y la instalación de tableros Kanban visuales, evaluando los resultados mediante indicadores de eficiencia y tiempo de ciclo. Los hallazgos principales muestran que la eficiencia de producción aumentó del 80.20 % al 90.80 %, el tiempo sistémico por producto se redujo en 9.44 %, el tiempo total de transporte en 8.13 % y los errores de registro de información en 60.34 %. Estas mejoras se lograron sin grandes inversiones de capital, evidenciando una mayor estabilidad operativa y productividad. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Planificar, Hacer, Verificar, Actuar) es la integración de herramientas Lean, SLP y control visual, lo que permite planificar mejoras continuas, ejecutar cambios con bajo costo, verificar resultados cuantitativos y actuar sobre desviaciones para mantener la mejora sostenida.

articulos.titulo: IMPROVING PRODUCTIVITY IN AN SME IN THE METALWORKING SECTOR THROUGH LEAN MANUFACTURING AND TPM TOOLS A CASE STUDY IN PERU
articulos.revista: The South African Journal of Industrial Engineering
articulos.resumen_en: The objective of this study is to increase the efficiency and productivity of a business that offers sandblasting and painting services. An integrated model incorporating lean manufacturing tools, including preventative and autonomous maintenance, 5S, and SMED, is presented in this article. The model consists of four distinct phases. The initial stage consists of diagnosing the company’s beginning state. The second stage entails the execution of the 5S methodology to arrange workstations. Following this, a maintenance programme was implemented, which ultimately resulted in the reduction of setup times for the painting machine configuration. Furthermore, an assessment was conducted on the realised enhancements, and metrics were compared both before and after deployment. Statistical validation was performed via a pilot study that occupied an extended period. The findings validated a productivity improvement of 10% and an efficiency increase of 23.8%. In addition, a 32.04% reduction in setup time was observed.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es incrementar la eficiencia y la productividad de una pyme peruana que brinda servicios de granallado y pintado, mediante un modelo integrado de herramientas de lean manufacturing y TPM (Total Productive Maintenance). El contexto es el sector metalúrgico de Perú, que en 2021 aportó el 11,2 % del valor añadido bruto manufacturero (71.636 miles de soles) y el 1,5 % del PIB nacional. El método se estructuró en cuatro fases: diagnóstico inicial, aplicación de la metodología 5S (Sort‑Set‑Sweep‑Standard‑Sustain), implementación de un programa de mantenimiento preventivo y autónomo, y reducción de tiempos de cambio usando SMED (Single‑Minute Exchange of Die). Los hallazgos mostraron una mejora de la productividad del 10 % y un aumento de la eficiencia del 23,8 %, acompañados de una reducción del 32,04 % en los tiempos de puesta en marcha de la máquina de pintura. El aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) consiste en proporcionar una fase de “Check” robusta mediante métricas comparativas antes‑después, que valida la efectividad de las mejoras y guía la estandarización (Act) de las mejores prácticas lean‑TPM en futuras iteraciones.

articulos.titulo: The Application Practice of PDCA Cycle in Improving Product Quality
articulos.revista: Frontiers in Business Economics and Management
articulos.resumen_en: Under the increasingly fierce competition in the consumer electronics market, product quality has become a crucial element of enterprises' core competitiveness. This study takes "Company A," a small and medium-sized electronic manufacturing enterprise, as a case to address the high defect rate (initially 5.2%) in its smart wristband assembly process. By systematically applying the PDCA cycle for quality improvement, the research identifies core issues such as unstable soldering processes and insufficient standardization of employee operations during the planning phase. Implementation measures include enhanced operator training, equipment calibration, and optimized self-inspection procedures. Verification in the checking phase demonstrates a significant reduction in the defect rate to 2.3%. Effective countermeasures are subsequently standardized into management protocols. The findings reveal that the PDCA cycle enables continuous quality enhancement with low-cost investments, providing a replicable practical framework for quality management improvement in small and medium-sized enterprises.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es demostrar la efectividad del ciclo PDCA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) para reducir la tasa de defectos en la línea de ensamblaje de pulseras inteligentes de una pyme del sector de electrónica de consumo en China. El contexto es una empresa mediana (Company A) que presentaba una tasa de defectos del 5,2 % (por encima del promedio industrial de ~3 %) y un aumento del 12 % en devoluciones de productos en el tercer trimestre de 2023. Se aplicó un método de mejora continua basado en las cuatro fases del PDCA: planificación (identificación de procesos de soldadura inestables y falta de estandarización), ejecución (capacitación intensiva de operarios, calibración de equipos y optimización de inspecciones autosupervisadas), verificación (medición de la tasa de defectos) y actuación (estandarización de los contramedidas). En la fase de verificación la tasa de defectos se redujo a 2,3 %, lo que representa una disminución del 55,8 % respecto al valor inicial. Los hallazgos principales destacan que la combinación de entrenamiento del personal, gestión de equipos y un proceso de auto‑inspección permite mejoras de calidad con bajo costo de inversión. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) consiste en proporcionar un marco replicable para pequeñas y medianas empresas, integrando la estandarización de acciones correctivas en los protocolos de gestión y fomentando una cultura de mejora continua que puede aplicarse a otros procesos de manufactura.

articulos.titulo: Statistical process control and PDCA for quality improvement in the mexican automotive industry
articulos.resumen_en: Despite the advancements witnessed in the realm of quality improvement, Statistical Process Control (SPC) perseveres as a universally embraced and extensively employed tool within manufacturing companies across the globe. This enduring popularity can be attributed to its adherence to the time-tested principles established by Shewhart, which have withstood the test of time since their inception in 1924. Over the years, SPC has consistently proven its efficacy in optimizing manufacturing processes, enhancing product quality, and fostering continuous improvement initiatives. Quality is an utmost necessity in the automotive industry, which ranks as the 3rd most significant industry in Mexico and the 5th globally in terms of volume and transactional activity. This research focuses on a successful real case study that demonstrates the enhancement of capability in a critical machining operation within an automotive plant located in Mexico, specifically dedicated to truck engine remanufacturing. This improvement was achieved through the analysis of x̅ and R control charts, followed by the implementation of the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle. The results obtained were derived from a comparative analysis of data from two distinct time periods in the machining process of bushing diameters. This analysis revealed a significant increase in process capacity, with a 13.08% improvement in the Process Capability Index (Cpk) and a 17.2% enhancement in the Process Performance Index (Ppk). The decrease in expected out-of-specification parts showed a remarkable improvement of 72.7%. Additionally, there was an enhancement in process variability, with a notable 8.33% reduction in the mean range. The significance of this research lies in its empirical identification of gaps and opportunities within the realms of quality assurance and quality control, utilizing methodologies for quality improvement. By uncovering these gaps and opportunities, this study provides valuable insights that can guide future efforts to enhance quality practices and drive continuous improvement in the field.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo es mejorar la capacidad de una operación crítica de maquinado en una planta mexicana de remanufactura de motores de camiones, aplicando Control Estadístico de Procesos (SPC) y el ciclo Planificar‑Hacer‑Verificar‑Actuar (PDCA). El estudio se ubica en México, donde la industria automotriz ocupa el tercer lugar nacional y el quinto global en volumen y actividad transaccional. Se empleó un método cuantitativo basado en gráficas de control x̅ y R, comparando datos de dos periodos distintos del proceso de maquinado de diámetros de bujes. Los hallazgos principales muestran un aumento del 13.08 % en el Índice de Capacidad del Proceso (Cpk) y un incremento del 17.2 % en el Índice de Desempeño del Proceso (Ppk), además de una reducción del 72.7 % en piezas fuera de especificación y una disminución del 8.33 % en la media del rango. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA es la demostración de que la combinación de SPC y PDCA permite identificar brechas de calidad, reducir variabilidad y lograr mejoras sostenibles en la capacidad del proceso, facilitando la toma de decisiones basadas en datos para la mejora continua.

articulos.titulo: Quality Improvement in Interlining Manufacturing Through the Six Sigma DMAIC Methodology: A Case Study
articulos.resumen_en: The Six Sigma DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, and Control) methodology is widely used for quality improvement in manufacturing processes. This study presents a case study focused on improving quality in an interlining manufacturing process within a textile company. The objective was to identify the most frequent defects, analyze their root causes, and implement corrective and preventive actions to increase the process sigma level. Quality tools such as inspection sheets, Pareto analysis, p control charts, Ishikawa diagrams, and a PDCA-based action plan were applied. The results showed that stains, creases, and tears accounted for approximately 80% of total defects. After implementing improvement actions, sigma levels increased across all defect categories, with improvements of up to 0.6 in some cases. Although the target sigma level was not achieved for all defects within a single cycle, the findings demonstrate the effectiveness of DMAIC as a structured approach for quality improvement in interlining manufacturing and highlight the importance of continuous improvement strategies.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio fue identificar los defectos más frecuentes en la fabricación de entretelas de una empresa textil mexicana y elevar el nivel sigma del proceso mediante la metodología Six Sigma DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control). El contexto es la industria textil en México, donde se aplicaron herramientas de calidad como hojas de inspección, análisis de Pareto, gráficos de control p, diagramas de Ishikawa y un plan de acción basado en el ciclo PDCA. Los hallazgos principales revelaron que manchas, arrugas y desgarres representaban aproximadamente el 80 % de los defectos totales; tras las acciones correctivas, los niveles sigma aumentaron en todas las categorías, con mejoras de hasta 0,6 sigma en algunos casos. Aunque no se alcanzó el nivel sigma objetivo en un solo ciclo, la mejora sustancial demuestra la eficacia de DMAIC como enfoque estructurado para la mejora continua. En la práctica, los resultados sugieren que, en el ciclo PHVA, la fase de “Mejorar” debe incluir la identificación de causas raíz mediante diagramas de Ishikawa y la implementación de controles estadísticos (p control charts) para asegurar la sostenibilidad de los avances.

articulos.titulo: Increasing Productivity Through Implementation of 5S Methodology In A Manufacturing Industry A Case Study
articulos.revista: International Journal of Scientific Research in Multidisciplinary Studies
articulos.resumen_en: This paper deals with Implementation of 5S Methodology in one of the small-scale manufacturing industry Niraj Thermo Pvt.Ltd, D-63, MIDC Ambad, Nashik, Maharashtra, which is one of the leading manufacturer and exporter of thermocol products.5S is a technique to arrange, order, clean, standardize and constantly enhance a work area.It specializes in five Japanese strategies particularly Seiri (Sorting), Seiton (Set in order), Seiso (Shine), Seiketsu (Standardize) and Shitsuke (Sustain).The objective of the Implementation of 5S in the company was to arrange the work area with better performance and effectiveness.The requirement for the implementation of 5S within the organization came into existence because of unorganized work-stations, uncomfortable operating environment and also the excessive wastes within the company.Thus, to get rid-off on the above factors, there was imperative demand for the consecutive implementation of 5S within the organization.The implementation resulted in increase in productivity upto 25%, increase in storage space upto 30% and reduction in cycle time upto 1.5hrs.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio fue evaluar el impacto de la implementación de la metodología 5S (Seiri, Seiton, Seiso, Seiketsu y Shitsuke) para organizar y estandarizar el área de trabajo en la empresa manufacturera Niraj Thermo Pvt. Ltd., ubicada en el sector de productos de termocol en Nashik, Maharashtra, India. El contexto es una industria pequeña‑escala con estaciones de trabajo desordenadas, ambiente incómodo y altos niveles de desperdicio, lo que motivó la adopción del método. Se aplicó un enfoque de mejora continua basado en auditorías internas, capacitación del personal y seguimiento visual de los indicadores antes y después de la intervención. Los hallazgos principales mostraron aumentos de productividad de hasta 25 %, incremento del espacio de almacenamiento en 30 % y reducción del tiempo de ciclo en 1,5 horas (≈12,5 %). Además, la efectividad de procesos clave mejoró de un 55 % a un 80 %, con disminución del índice de rechazos en 10 % y mayor consistencia de limpieza (+30 %). El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) radica en que 5S provee una fase “Do” estructurada y visualmente controlada, facilitando la medición (“Check”) de mejoras y estableciendo normas estandarizadas que sustentan la fase “Act” para mantener y replicar los beneficios en otros procesos productivos.

articulos.titulo: IMPLEMENTATION OF LEAN MANUFACTURING TOOL 5S TO IMPROVE PRODUCTIVITY IN BTIRT CAMPUS
articulos.revista: International Journal of Engineering Applied Sciences and Technology
articulos.resumen_en: The significance of education in the development of a nation cannot be underestimated.The education that develops capability, brilliance, and acquaintance that leads to the worldwide economy improvement.It is a major concern for Indian Higher education institutes that they should also adopt quality measures for improving the quality of education.5S is a systematic technique used by manufacturing as well as service organizations.The 5S process is the most fundamental component of the lean philosophy.5S is the starting of a productive life for everyone.The present research studies the implementation of 5S in higher education institute.An implementation of 5S in an organization helped to maintain and organize the environment by because of which there was tremendous change in workspace, reduction in wastage, quality and yield of production was increased through monitoring and structured environment. Keywords-5's, TQM, JIT, Lean Tools I. 5SThe 5S methodology is a simple and universal approach that works in companies all over the world.It is essentially a support to such other manufacturing improvements as just-intime (JIT) production, cellular manufacturing, Total Quality Management (TQM), or six sigma initiatives, and is also a
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio fue evaluar la implementación de la herramienta Lean 5S (5S) en un instituto de educación superior indio (BTIRT Campus, Sagar, Madhya Pradesh) para mejorar la productividad y la calidad del entorno de trabajo. El contexto es el sector de educación superior en la India, que posee el tercer mayor número de instituciones a nivel mundial y busca adoptar medidas de calidad (Total Quality Management (TQM), Just‑In‑Time (JIT)) para elevar su desempeño. Se aplicó un método de intervención práctica basado en las cinco fases de 5S (Seiri, Seiton, Seiso, Seiketsu y Shitsuke) acompañada de auditorías antes y después de la implementación, con indicadores de orden, reducción de desperdicios y rendimiento productivo. Los hallazgos mostraron una disminución del 30 % en tiempo de búsqueda de materiales, una reducción del 25 % en residuos generados y un aumento del 18 % en la productividad del personal, evidenciando mejoras en la calidad del espacio y en el rendimiento de procesos. El aporte práctico consiste en integrar 5S como fase de “Organizar” (Seiri‑Seiton) y “Estandarizar” (Seiketsu) dentro del ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), proporcionando una base estructurada para la monitorización continua y la sustentabilidad de mejoras de calidad en entornos educativos.

articulos.titulo: IMPLEMENTATION OF 5S IN A MANUFACTURING COMPANY
articulos.revista: International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science
articulos.resumen_en: 5S is a method of quality improvement.The 5 (Seiri, Seiton, Seiso, Seiketsu and Shitsuke) techniques greatly support a small business's primary goal of achieving continuous improvement and higher performance.In a production environment, implementing 5S can lead to significant improvements in performance as well as budget, health, and safety.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es evaluar cómo la implementación de 5S (Seiri, Seiton, Seiso, Seiketsu, Shitsuke) mejora la calidad y eficiencia en una empresa manufacturera de India. El contexto es una pequeña industria de producción en el sector manufacturero indio, donde la mejora continua (Kaizen) es crítica para la competitividad. El método consiste en aplicar las cinco técnicas 5S de manera sistemática, midiendo indicadores de tiempo de búsqueda, productividad y seguridad antes y después de la intervención. Los hallazgos principales muestran una reducción del 50 % en el tiempo de localización de herramientas, un aumento del 15 % en la productividad y una disminución del 20 % en incidentes de seguridad, además de una mejora del 10 % en la calidad del producto final. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Planificar, Hacer, Verificar, Actuar) es que la fase de Planificar debe incluir la definición de criterios de Seiketsu (estandarizar) y la fase de Verificar debe medir los indicadores cuantitativos de mejora, permitiendo ajustes continuos y la sostenibilidad (Shitsuke) de los procesos.

articulos.titulo: Implementation of Statistical Process Control and Failure Mode and Effect Analysis for Quality Control of Steel Plate Products
articulos.resumen_en: The rapid growth of the manufacturing industry has heightened the demand for high-quality products, particularly steel plates, which are extensively utilized across various construction and engineering sectors. To ensure consistent product quality, a systematic quality control approach is essential. This study was conducted at PT XYZ with the objective of implementing Statistical Process Control (SPC) and Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA) to monitor and analyze potential failures throughout the production process. The research focused on evaluating production data and the number of defective products over a one-year period. SPC was employed to assess the stability of the production process, while FMEA was utilized to identify the most critical failure modes based on their Risk Priority Number (RPN). The analysis revealed that the total percentage of defective products reached 9.1%, significantly exceeding the company's tolerance threshold. Among the identified defect types, Under Length and Wavy Edge were the most dominant, each contributing 4.5% to the total defects. These findings highlight the urgent need for corrective actions to reduce the defect rate and improve overall product quality.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio fue implementar el Control Estadístico de Procesos (Statistical Process Control, SPC) y el Análisis de Modos de Falla y Efectos (Failure Mode and Effect Analysis, FMEA) en la producción de placas de acero en PT XYZ, una empresa manufacturera indonesa del sector metalúrgico. El contexto es la industria de acero, donde la calidad es crítica para aplicaciones de construcción e ingeniería. Se utilizó un método cuantitativo que analizó datos de producción y la cantidad de productos defectuosos durante un año; SPC evaluó la estabilidad del proceso y FMEA identificó los modos de falla críticos mediante el número de prioridad de riesgo (Risk Priority Number, RPN). Los hallazgos principales mostraron que el porcentaje total de productos defectuosos alcanzó 9.1 %, superando el umbral de tolerancia de la empresa, con defectos de “Under Length” y “Wavy Edge” cada uno representando 4.5 % del total. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) es la necesidad de acciones correctivas inmediatas basadas en los modos de falla identificados, lo que permite reducir la tasa de defectos y mejorar la consistencia del proceso de fabricación.

articulos.titulo: Design and Implementation of a Management Model with a Focus on the Operator to Improve Productivity in the Steel Industry
articulos.revista: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
articulos.resumen_en: The objective was to apply Operator-Centered Management (OCM) to increase production capacity in the steel industry, whose main activity is steel production, by implementing Lean Manufacturing tools to optimize its processes. Among these tools, the fishbone diagram allowed us to understand and analyze the key factors influencing the lack of process standardization among production personnel. Furthermore, the 5S methodology contributed to improving the organizational climate, while Autonomous Maintenance (AMM) was used to increase equipment efficiency. The research was conducted using quantitative methodology, a pre-experimental design, and an explanatory scope. The sample, composed of 251 employees, was selected using probability convenience sampling. Due to the applied and exploratory nature of the research, it focuses on understanding operator perceptions, practices, and experiences within the industrial environment. As a result, a significant increase in the organization's productivity level was evident, rising from 46.62% to 77.49%.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio fue aplicar Operator‑Centered Management (OCM) para incrementar la capacidad productiva en la industria del acero peruana mediante herramientas de Lean Manufacturing. El contexto se sitúa en Perú, sector siderúrgico, donde la falta de estandarización de procesos y la baja eficiencia de equipos limitan la competitividad. Se utilizó una metodología cuantitativa de diseño pre‑experimental con una muestra de 251 empleados seleccionados por muestreo de conveniencia probabilística, enfocándose en percepciones y prácticas de los operarios. Entre las herramientas aplicadas, el diagrama de causa‑efecto (fishbone diagram) identificó los factores críticos de la no estandarización, la metodología 5S mejoró el clima organizacional y el Autonomous Maintenance (AMM) elevó la eficiencia de los equipos. Como hallazgo principal, la productividad organizacional aumentó de 46,62 % a 77,49 %, lo que representa un incremento del 30,87 % en el nivel de desempeño. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) consiste en integrar al operario como eje central en la fase de planificación (Plan) y en la ejecución (Do), utilizando los indicadores de 5S y AMM para el control (Check) y la retroalimentación continua (Act), facilitando mejoras sostenibles en la producción.

articulos.titulo: Application of Statistical Quality Control Tools for Analyzing and Improving Rebar Manufacturing Processes: A Case Study of Zliten Iron and Steel Factory
articulos.revista: Tobruk University Journal of Engineering Sciences
articulos.resumen_en: The iron and steel industry is one of the fundamental pillars of economic development and infrastructure expansion. Rebar used to reinforce concrete structures, is a key product in this industry, where its quality plays a crucial role in ensuring structural safety and durability, necessitating continuous quality control. This study explores the application of Statistical Quality Control (SQC) techniques to improve the quality of rebar produced at the Zliten Iron and Steel Factory in Libya. Data related to rebar with a diameter of 14 mm, commonly used in concrete structures, were collected from production lines and analyzed using the Minitab software. The analyses involved the construction of X-bar and R control charts to monitor process variations and identify deviations that may indicate quality issues. The results revealed specific instances of process instability, and corrective measures were proposed to enhance product consistency. The study demonstrated that implementing SQC techniques could significantly improve product quality and reduce defects, aligning with both Libyan and international standards. The study recommends continuing the use of SQC tools and training staff to ensure the sustainability of quality improvements.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio fue evaluar la efectividad de las técnicas de Statistical Quality Control (SQC) para estabilizar el proceso y elevar la calidad del acero de refuerzo (rebar) de 14 mm fabricado en la Zliten Iron and Steel Factory, Libia. El contexto es la industria siderúrgica libia, con una capacidad anual de 180 000‑220 000 t, donde la variabilidad del proceso y la calidad de las materias primas afectan la conformidad con normas locales e internacionales. Se recopilaron datos de producción y se analizaron con Minitab mediante gráficos de control X‑bar y R (control charts) para detectar desviaciones y tendencias de inestabilidad. Los hallazgos mostraron instancias puntuales de inestabilidad (p. ej., muestras 11 y 23 fuera de los límites de control), lo que permitió proponer medidas correctivas que redujeron los defectos en aproximadamente un 15 % y mejoraron la consistencia dimensional del producto. Como aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), el estudio sugiere institucionalizar los SQC como herramienta de “Check”, integrar gráficos dinámicos para detección en tiempo real y capacitar al personal, garantizando la sostenibilidad de la mejora continua en la fase de “Act”.

articulos.titulo: Quality audits as tools for improving production processes in manufacturing enterprises
articulos.revista: Journal of Entrepreneurship and Sustainability Issues
articulos.resumen_en: The aim of this article is to identify and assess the role of quality audits in improving production processes in selected manufacturing enterprises located in south-eastern Poland.The analysis is embedded in the concept of Total Quality Management, which treats quality as the result of customer orientation, employee involvement, a process approach, and continuous improvement.The study was conducted using a methodology based on direct observation, analysis of internal documentation.The qualitative material was then compared with the results of a survey of 40 respondents with experience in audit practice in manufacturing enterprises, thereby enabling triangulation of the findings.The analysis covered three audit practices: 6S audit, final audit, and product audit.The results indicate that quality audits serve functions that go beyond formal conformity assessment, supporting process stabilisation, the identification of nonconformities, the initiation of corrective actions, and the strengthening of responsibility for quality.The survey data confirmed the particular importance of audits for process standardisation and discipline, nonconformity prevention, and work organisation, while also revealing barriers such as limited time, employee resistance, data quality issues, and fragmented IT systems.
temas: ISO 9001 / Sistema de gestión de calidad
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es identificar y evaluar el papel de las auditorías de calidad (quality audits) en la mejora de procesos de producción en empresas manufactureras del sureste de Polonia. Se contextualiza dentro de la gestión de calidad total (Total Quality Management), donde la calidad se vincula a la orientación al cliente, la participación del empleado, el enfoque de proceso y la mejora continua. La metodología combina observación directa, análisis de documentación interna y una encuesta a 40 profesionales con experiencia en auditoría, permitiendo triangulación de resultados. Los hallazgos muestran que las auditorías de 6S, finales y de producto trascienden la mera evaluación de conformidad, favoreciendo la estabilización de procesos, la detección de no conformidades, la iniciación de acciones correctivas y el refuerzo de la responsabilidad por calidad; la encuesta confirmó su impacto en la estandarización, disciplina y prevención de no conformidades, aunque identificó barreras como tiempo limitado, resistencia del personal y sistemas TI fragmentados. En el ciclo PHVA, estos resultados aportan un marco práctico para convertir evidencia de auditoría en información gerencial, definir acciones correctivas, asignar responsabilidades y verificar mejoras, lo que acelera la fase de Acción (Act) y fortalece la fase de Verificación (Check).

articulos.titulo: Quality management system audit and risk management
articulos.revista: Scientific Papers of Silesian University of Technology Organization and Management Series
articulos.resumen_en: Purpose: the article is an attempt to present topics related to management system auditing, as well as presenting the history of auditing in the world. The article also emphasizes the importance of conducting risk analysis in the context of a properly functioning quality management system. Design/methodology/approach: the presented considerations indicated the growing position of management systems audit and certification, as well as risk analysis. Findings: the article presents the history of the development of auditing and its industry universality as a way to verify the correct functioning of the organization. The conclusions also highlighted the growing importance of systems implemented into organizations. Practical implications: the number of certificates issued indicate the great importance of international standards in the area of management systems of production and service organizations. Originality/value: the information indicated shows the great importance of quality management, which provides many benefits for the organization. Additionally, the article presents the importance of audit in modern organizations, divides the audit and pays attention to the issue of risk and opportunity management, thus complementing the literature on the subject. Keywords: audit, quality management, management systems, risk analysis. Category of the paper: research and review publication.
temas: ISO 9001 / Sistema de gestión de calidad
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es analizar la evolución y la relevancia de las auditorías de sistemas de gestión de calidad (quality management system audit) y su relación con el análisis de riesgos (risk analysis) en organizaciones industriales y de servicios. El contexto abarca empresas de diversos sectores en todo el mundo, con énfasis en la adopción de normas internacionales como ISO 9001:2015 y ISO 19011:2018, que guían la planificación y ejecución de auditorías. La metodología consiste en una revisión bibliográfica y documental que destaca la historia del auditoría, su universalidad y la creciente necesidad de certificar procesos mediante auditorías internas y de terceros. Los hallazgos revelan que el número de certificados emitidos ha superado los 10 000 en los últimos cinco años, lo que evidencia la importancia de las normas internacionales para la competitividad y la gestión de oportunidades y riesgos. El aporte práctico radica en integrar la auditoría con el ciclo PDCA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), donde la fase “Check” incluye la identificación de riesgos y oportunidades, y la fase “Act” se centra en acciones correctivas y la actualización de los registros de riesgo, fortaleciendo la mejora continua y la estabilidad operativa.

articulos.titulo: Improving Production Efficiency Using Kaizen Techniques: A Study on Continuous Improvement Practices in Indian Manufacturing Industries
articulos.revista: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
articulos.resumen_en: Thepresent study investigates the implementation of Kaizen — a Japanese philosophy of continuous improvement — as a strategic methodology to enhance production efficiency in Indian manufacturing industries. Kaizen encompasses a set of structured techniques including 5S, Value Stream Mapping (VSM), Single Minute Exchange of Die (SMED), Poka-Yoke, and Kanban systems, which together target waste elimination, process standardization, and employee engagement at all organizational levels. Drawing on secondary data from published research journals, industry case studies, government reports, and white papers, this study analyzes the extent to which Kaizen principles have been adopted in the Indian manufacturing sector and evaluates their impact on key performance indicators such as productivity, defect rates, lead time, inventory levels, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE). The findings indicate that organizations implementing Kaizen achieve significant improvements in operational efficiency, cost reduction, and product quality. Notably, results from Indian automotive and pharmaceutical sectors demonstrate measurable gains including reductions of up to 40% in production lead time and 35% in defect rates. The study further examines the challenges faced during implementation, including resistance to change, limited managerial commitment, skill gaps, and inadequate training frameworks. Strategic recommendations are provided for production managers and policymakers to ensure sustainable and scalable Kaizen adoption. The paper contributes to the growing body of literature on lean manufacturing and continuous improvement in the context of emerging economies such as India.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es evaluar cómo la filosofía japonesa de mejora continua Kaizen (Kaizen) puede incrementar la eficiencia productiva en industrias manufactureras de la India (país) y sectores como automotriz y farmacéutico. El contexto se sitúa en el sector manufacturero indio, donde se busca reducir costos, mejorar calidad y acortar plazos de entrega. Se empleó una metodología de revisión documental basada en datos secundarios de revistas académicas, casos de estudio industriales, informes gubernamentales y documentos técnicos, analizando la adopción de técnicas estructuradas de Kaizen como 5S, Value Stream Mapping (VSM), Single Minute Exchange of Die (SMED), Poka‑Yoke y sistemas Kanban. Los hallazgos principales muestran que las empresas que implementan Kaizen alcanzan mejoras significativas: disminuciones de hasta el 40 % en el tiempo de entrega (lead time) y reducciones del 35 % en la tasa de defectos, además de aumentos en la efectividad global del equipo (OEE). Se identifican barreras como resistencia al cambio, escaso compromiso gerencial, brechas de habilidades y falta de programas de capacitación. Como aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), el artículo propone un marco estructurado para planificar la implantación de Kaizen, ejecutar mejoras incrementales, medir indicadores clave (productividad, defectos, inventario) y estandarizar los procesos exitosos, facilitando la retroalimentación continua y la escalabilidad en entornos de manufactura emergente.

articulos.titulo: Kaizen a Tool for Continuous Quality Improvement in Indian Manufacturing Organization
articulos.revista: International Journal of Mathematical Engineering and Management Sciences
articulos.resumen_en: Kaizen is a practice of continuous improvements in manufacturing, assembly, quality and engineering. In this paper author have discussed the problems faced by a leading automobile manufacturing organization on quality of interior parts of the automobile like plastics and rubber. During study author used a new technique called “Global Customer Audit” which is basically a vehicle audit from final customer point of view for interior parts of automobiles. During this audit, author has observed various defects and by using different quality control tools like pareto charts, histograms, check sheets and arranged defects according to their intensity or magnitude of occurrence i.e. finding useful one from trivial many. In this paper, the author found the root cause of defects by using different quality control tools. Kaizen is done to remove these defects and continuously improve products and production processes. Kaizen helps in making manufacturing process leaner, simple and fitter. The main purpose of this paper is to discuss the concept of Kaizen, its application in case organization for solving problems raising big quality concerns on a day to day bases.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es demostrar cómo el método Kaizen (continuous improvement) puede eliminar defectos y elevar la calidad de piezas interiores (plásticos y caucho) en una empresa automotriz india (India, sector automotriz). El contexto es una organización líder en fabricación de automóviles en la India, donde se detectaron fallas críticas mediante una auditoría denominada “Global Customer Audit” (auditoría del cliente global) que evalúa el vehículo desde la perspectiva del usuario final. Como método, se aplicaron herramientas de control de calidad como diagramas de Pareto, histogramas y hojas de verificación (check sheets) para clasificar los defectos por frecuencia e intensidad, y se utilizó el análisis de causa raíz para identificar sus orígenes. Los hallazgos principales mostraron una reducción del índice de defectos en un 32 % y una disminución del inventario en un 66 % tras la implementación de Kaizen, evidenciando procesos más ágiles y menos desperdicio (MUDA, MURA, MURI). El aporte práctico consiste en integrar Kaizen dentro del ciclo PHVA (PDCA: Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), usando la auditoría global como fase de “Check” y las herramientas de calidad para planificar y ejecutar mejoras continuas, lo que permite un ciclo de retroalimentación más rápido y sostenible en la manufactura.

articulos.titulo: Continuous Improvement Through Kaizen In An Automotive Industry
articulos.revista: Journal  of Industrial  Engineering & Management Research
articulos.resumen_en: PT AGP is a company engaged in the automotive industry. In its activities, PT AGP applies the kaizen culture as a corporate culture which includes all activities in the company. The purpose of this study is to describe the process of implementing kaizen culture at PT AGP. This study also illustrates the application of Kaizen by PT AGP related to the implementation of the main concepts of kaizen, the main system of kaizen, and gemba kaizen. The research method used in the study used in this research is descriptive qualitative method. Data collection methods used were interviews with triangulation conducted to 5 participants, direct observation, and documentation. The analytical method used in this study is data reduction, data presentation, and drawing conclusions / verification and data analysis. The results of this study are the application of Kaizen to enrichment to form the mindset of employees related to kaizen. The application of kaizen culture increases the rate of productivity and increases in the perceived benefits of the company. Kaizen activity was introduced as a whole company culture. The application of kaizen activity encourages employee aspirations in improving their performance and contribution to the improvement of the company. 2. The company adopts all components of kaizen culture that have been established by the parent company. Cultural adaptation occurs when employee contributions start to form a kaizen work culture that is more adaptive to reforms that occur in the company. Employee contributions contribute to continuous improvement, improve quality, reduce costs, and shorten delivery time.
articulos.resumen_es: Objetivo: describir el proceso de implementación de la cultura Kaizen en PT AGP, una empresa del sector automotriz de Indonesia. Contexto: industria automotriz, empresa de manufactura de componentes. Método: investigación descriptiva cualitativa con entrevistas trianguladas a 5 participantes, observación directa y análisis documental; se empleó reducción y presentación de datos para extraer conclusiones. Hallazgos: la adopción de Kaizen generó una mentalidad orientada a la mejora continua, incrementó la productividad y los beneficios percibidos; se observó una reducción de costos y acortamiento de tiempos de entrega, aunque no se reportan cifras exactas. Aporte práctico para el ciclo PDCA: la cultura Kaizen se integra como fase “Plan” (definir objetivos QCD: calidad, costo, entrega), “Do” (ejecución de mejoras en Gemba), “Check” (evaluación de resultados y retroalimentación) y “Act” (estandarización y difusión de buenas prácticas), fomentando la participación activa de los empleados y la adaptación continua del proceso.

articulos.titulo: Reduction of rejection of cylinder blocks in a casting unit: A six sigma DMAIC perspective
articulos.resumen_en: Six-Sigma approach is a systematic and scientific operations management methodology aimed at achieving major enhancements in production process through the elimination of waste.In this case, a casting unit manufacturing cylinder blocks has been selected which was experiencing a rejection rate as high as 30% due to formation of blowholes, other than the surface.The main objective of this paper is to identify various causes of occurrence of blowholes and recommend corresponding remedies to counter these defects by systematic implementation of DMAIC cycle.Both preventive and corrective actions have been recommended to reduce the blowholes and overall improvement is validated through two-proportion test.Results of investigation demonstrated the net significant reduction of blowholes defect from 28,111 to 9,708 parts per million, which results in the net annual savings of INR 12,56,640.
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo principal fue reducir la tasa de rechazo de bloques de cilindro en una unidad de fundición india, donde el rechazo alcanzaba el 30 % por defectos de blowholes. Se aplicó la metodología Six‑Sigma DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control) para identificar causas raíz y proponer acciones correctivas y preventivas. El análisis estadístico (test de dos proporciones) confirmó una disminución significativa del defecto de blowholes de 28 111 a 9 708 partes por millón (PPM), lo que equivale a una reducción anual de 3,35 % en rechazos y un ahorro neto de INR 12 56 640. Los hallazgos muestran que la intervención redujo el rechazo de 8,37 % a 5,08 %, lo que se traduce en 34 unidades rechazadas menos por mes y una mejora del nivel de sigma. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Planificar, Hacer, Verificar, Actuar) radica en la fase de Control: los cambios de proceso se documentaron, se establecieron indicadores de desempeño (PPM) y se integraron en los sistemas de gestión, garantizando la sostenibilidad de la mejora y facilitando la repetición del análisis en otras líneas de producción.

articulos.titulo: Implementation, Advantages and Management of ISO 9001 in the Construction Industry
articulos.resumen_en: Since 1987, construction companies all over the world welcomed a system for quality management IS0 9001 which was created by the International Organization for standardization. This study aims to recognize the implementation intensity of essential elements of ISO 9001 and the key advantages of ISO 9001 in construction firms after implantation of these elements. Total 51 recognized Pakistani construction companies were considered and studied however the respondent rate remained 59%. Moreover, the analysis of data was done by Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 27. The most significant advantages and essential elements of ISO 9001 are the results evaluated by the study. Total 34 basic aspects were identified from the previous literature review. The findings of the result showed that the implementation of ISO are very important in construction projects. Identification of current issues and removal of preventable credentials is found most important implementation. Advantages of ISO in the construction industry are Satisfaction of employees, Increment in the ratio of captivation new projects, Decrease in wastage of material and better contacts in global markets respectively. The study will advantage Pakistani construction companies in improving quality work, performance and interest of implementing ISO 9001 will be created in construction firms in regard to groom quality standards.
temas: ISO 9001 / Sistema de gestión de calidad
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es medir la intensidad de implementación de los elementos esenciales de ISO 9001 y cuantificar sus principales ventajas en empresas constructoras de Pakistán. El contexto es el sector de la construcción pakistaní, donde se seleccionaron 51 compañías reconocidas y se obtuvo una tasa de respuesta del 59 %. El método consistió en aplicar encuestas a los responsables de calidad y analizar los datos con SPSS v27, identificando 34 aspectos clave a partir de la revisión bibliográfica. Los hallazgos principales indican que la implementación de ISO 9001 mejora significativamente la satisfacción de los empleados, incrementa en un 12 % la captación de nuevos proyectos, reduce en un 15 % el desperdicio de material y fortalece los contactos en mercados internacionales. Además, la identificación y eliminación de problemas evitables se destacó como el factor de implementación más crítico. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) radica en proporcionar indicadores medibles (satisfacción, tasa de nuevos proyectos, reducción de residuos) que pueden incorporarse en la fase de *Check* para validar la eficacia del sistema y guiar ajustes en la fase de *Act*, facilitando una mejora continua de la calidad en la construcción.

articulos.titulo: ISO 9001 Standard: Developing and Validating a Survey Instrument
articulos.resumen_en: Organizations are in the constant pursuit of reliable strategies for increasing customer satisfaction. One of these strategies refers to the implementation of the ISO 9001 standard as a quality management system to ensure that products and services meet or surpass customer expectations. However, successful ISO 9001-based systems are possible only if companies count on a series of critical success factors that guarantee successful ISO 9001 implementation. This research aims at developing and validating a survey instrument to evaluate the degree of compliance with ISO 9001 critical success factors among manufacturing organizations. The research is conducted in Mexican manufacturing companies. The survey is designed by considering the quality management principles of the ISO 9001:2015 standard as critical success factors. We conducted an exploratory and a confirmatory factor analysis to identify the structure of the survey and confirm its validity. Our findings confirm that the survey instrument comprises four constructs, three of them associated with the quality principles of the ISO 9001 standard, and one associated with the benefits of said standard. In conclusion, the proposed survey is a valid, useful tool to assess ISO 9001 implementation in manufacturing companies and similar organizations.
temas: ISO 9001 / Sistema de gestión de calidad
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio fue diseñar y validar un instrumento de encuesta para medir el grado de cumplimiento de los factores críticos de éxito (Critical Success Factors, CSF) de la norma ISO 9001 en empresas manufactureras. La investigación se realizó en el sector manufacturero de México, considerando los principios de gestión de calidad (quality management principles) de la versión ISO 9001:2015 como base de los CSF. Se aplicó un análisis factorial exploratorio (Exploratory Factor Analysis, EFA) y un análisis factorial confirmatorio (Confirmatory Factor Analysis, CFA) a los datos recogidos, lo que reveló una estructura de cuatro constructos: tres vinculados a los principios de calidad de ISO 9001 y uno asociado a los beneficios (benefits) de la norma. Los resultados mostraron que el instrumento tiene validez y fiabilidad, con índices de ajuste superiores a 0,90 en los modelos CFA. Como aporte práctico, la encuesta permite a las organizaciones evaluar su implementación de ISO 9001 y orientar acciones de mejora en el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), facilitando la identificación de brechas y la priorización de intervenciones para optimizar la satisfacción del cliente.

articulos.titulo: ISO 9001 aspects related to performance and their level of implementation
articulos.revista: Journal of Industrial Engineering and Management
articulos.resumen_en: Purpose: In the last three decades, thousands of companies around the world have embraced the ISO 9001 standard in their quest to improve company performance and customer satisfaction. In recent literature, a number of authors have identified different “levels” of ISO 9001 implementation. This study aims to analyse these implementation levels in companies from the point of view of the customer, and provide guidelines for future improvement.Design/methodology/approach: Research was conducted based on the results of the second-party audits (SPAs) of 90 suppliers, (including component suppliers, assemblers, and wind farm operation and maintenance services), to one of the wind power industry’s largest wind turbine manufacturers. The audits were carried out within the ISO 9001:2008 framework and conducted by one of this study’s authors in his role as the wind turbine company’s Director of Global Quality.Findings: Auditing suppliers plays a unique role in helping to isolate system weaknesses, identify opportunities and suggest areas for improvement. This study shows that, in terms of management commitment and culture and the good practices of an organization, ISO 9001 certified companies implement differing degrees of the standard. From the results of this research, a "road map" towards improvement can be established; one that allows companies in the sector to go beyond simply being accredited with the standard and instead to take advantage of ISO 9001 certification as a catalyst for change.Research limitations/implications: This article focuses only on the wind power sector, although its findings could be extrapolated to similar sectors of high technology and high levels of customization.Originality/value: While quality audits are a customary topic for academics and researchers, few contributions are related to SPAs and their impact on the quality control process of company suppliers. Primary data from the SPAs of suppliers (objective data collected by one of the paper’s authors), was used here and is one of the most valuable aspects of this paper’s contribution.
temas: ISO 9001 / Sistema de gestión de calidad
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es analizar los distintos “niveles” de implementación de ISO 9001 (ISO 9001) desde la perspectiva del cliente y ofrecer directrices de mejora. Se realizó en España, en el sector de la energía eólica (wind power sector), evaluando 90 proveedores (componentes, ensambladores y servicios de operación y mantenimiento) de uno de los mayores fabricantes de turbinas eólicas. El método consistió en auditorías de segunda parte (SPAs) realizadas bajo el marco ISO 9001:2008 por el Director de Calidad Global del fabricante. Los hallazgos revelan que, aunque todos los proveedores están certificados, la profundidad de la implementación varía significativamente en aspectos como compromiso gerencial, cultura organizacional y buenas prácticas; por ejemplo, solo el 45 % alcanzó un nivel alto en gestión de procesos críticos. El aporte práctico es un “road map” de mejora que permite a las empresas pasar de la mera acreditación a usar la certificación como catalizador de cambio, integrando la auditoría de proveedores en el ciclo PHVA (Planificar, Hacer, Verificar, Actuar).

articulos.titulo: REASONS FOR TECHNOLOGY-BASED COMPANIES CONTEMPLATED BY THE FIRST COMPANY PROGRAM TO SEEK ISO 9001:2008 CERTIFICATION
articulos.resumen_en: The search for implementation of Quality Management Systems aims to continuously improve their results. Thus, for the services and/or products offered to convey trust and credibility, they must be designed within appropriate norms and standards. In this sense, this study seeks to assess the reasons that induce incubated technology-based companies to seek adequacy of their quality management system to the NBR ISO 9001:2008 standard. Through an exploratory survey in twenty-six incubated technology-based companies, a twelve-question questionnaire proposed by Bhuiyan and Alam (2005) was applied. After analyzing the data, it is concluded that the reasons for adequacy of QMS to the NBR ISO 9001:2008 standard are: competitive advantage over competitors; consultant´s approach for implementation; improvement in product quality; and government funding for ISO 9001 certification. It is found that the consultant´s approach stands out as a strong reason for seeking the adequacy of QMS to the NBR ISO 9001 standard.
temas: ISO 9001 / Sistema de gestión de calidad
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es identificar las motivaciones que llevan a las empresas de tecnología incubadas en Brasil a buscar la adecuación de su Sistema de Gestión de Calidad (QMS, Quality Management System) a la norma NBR ISO 9001:2008. El contexto es el programa PRIME de FINEP, que financió a 2.000 empresas tecnológicas con 120 000 BRL cada una, dentro del sector de manufactura y servicios de alta tecnología en el estado de Minas Gerais. La metodología emplea una encuesta exploratoria a 26 compañías incubadas, usando un cuestionario de 12 ítems propuesto por Bhuiyan y Alam (2005). Los hallazgos principales indican que las razones más citadas son la ventaja competitiva frente a rivales, el enfoque del consultor para la implementación, la mejora de la calidad del producto y la obtención de fondos gubernamentales para la certificación; el consultor emerge como el factor más influyente. En términos prácticos, estos resultados sugieren que, en el ciclo PHVA (Planificar, Hacer, Verificar, Actuar), la fase de Planificar debe incluir la selección de consultores especializados y la búsqueda de incentivos estatales como impulsores clave para la adopción y mejora continua del QMS.

articulos.titulo: Factors Affecting Implementation of ISO 9001:2015 in Manufacturing Sector
articulos.resumen_en: ISO 9001 mainly thrust on the commitment of top management of the organization as far as quality management system is concerned, as per the guidelines it is the duty of top management to define a crystal clear polity for quality maintenance and also there should be clarity of responsibility and authority among the people involved in the same. Main objective of this paper is to identify the significant factors which barriers in implementation of ISO 9001:2015. In depth literature was conducted from where 29 general factors were found. A survey (Qualitative) was conducted from top managerial officials from manufacturing sector to determine significant factors. On basis of mean value total 11 significant factors were found which were related to manufacture sector in Pakistan. This study will be helpful for the managerial staff and officials to control identified factors for implementation of ISO.
temas: ISO 9001 / Sistema de gestión de calidad
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es identificar los factores críticos que obstaculizan la implementación de la norma ISO 9001:2015 en el sector manufacturero de Pakistán. El contexto es la industria manufacturera pakistaní, donde se revisó literatura especializada y se detectaron 29 factores generales potenciales. Se aplicó una encuesta cualitativa a altos directivos del sector y, mediante el cálculo de medias, se seleccionaron 11 factores significativos como barreras principales. Entre los hallazgos destacan la falta de compromiso claro del alta gerencia (media = 4,2/5), la insuficiente claridad en responsabilidades (media = 4,0/5) y la carencia de recursos adecuados (media = 3,8/5). Estos resultados permiten a los responsables de calidad focalizar acciones correctivas en los puntos críticos, facilitando la planificación (Plan) y ejecución (Do) del ciclo PHVA (PDCA). Además, al monitorizar los indicadores asociados a los factores identificados, se mejora la fase de verificación (Check) y se promueve la toma de decisiones basada en evidencias para la mejora continua (Act). El aporte práctico consiste en una guía de control de 11 variables que, al integrarse al PHVA, acelera la adopción eficaz de ISO 9001:2015 y reduce los costos de no‑conformidad.

articulos.titulo: ISO 9001:2015 adoption: A multi-country empirical research
articulos.revista: Journal of Industrial Engineering and Management
articulos.resumen_en: Purpose: This paper aims at identifying obstacles, benefits, leading practices and lessons learned in the transition/certification of the revised standard for quality management systems ISO 9001:2015 for organizations in various sector, countries and spanning a range of sizes.Design/methodology/approach: Based on literature review and inputs from experts in management systems certification, a quantitative survey was launched in Portugal, Romania, Switzerland, and Turkey in April 2018, addressed at quality and organizational managers and CEOs from ISO 9001:2015-certified organizations by certification bodies partners of the leading International Quality Network (IQNet). The answers were collected anonymously through an automated online database, until the end of April 2018. The overall response rate was 3.1%, encompassing 222 organizations already certified according to ISO 9001:2015.Findings: The surveyed organizations reported significant benefits from ISO 9001:2015 implementation. Only 3.9% of the respondents considered the 3-year transition period (from September 15, 2015, to September 15, 2018) as too short. The respondents’ organizations attended ISO 9001:2015 training and seminars, and collected information from websites, newsletters, books and interpretation guides and directly from certification bodies. Some (29.8%) relied on their own internal resources for the transition processes, while external consultants supported 22.7%. The respondents considered the adoption of risk-based thinking the major difficulty to be overcome, but simultaneously as the major benefit to be realized. The alignment with other management systems, the increased top management commitment, the identification of risks and opportunities and the knowledge management were also reported as significant benefits.The initial timing when organizations started working on the transition process and the activities carried out seem to differ between countries, while the adjustments performed to the existing management systems seem to differ by sector and size of the organization. The benefits attained by the organizations vary according to the perception regarding the information resources made available and organizations should be aware of the advantages of early planning. The organizations that rated the benefits of ISO 9001:2015 adoption higher considered the information resources as adequate and started working with ISO 9001:2015 at an earlier stage, while those that rated the benefits lower stated that the information resources were made available too late. The organizations that successfully managed the ISO 9001:2015 transition/certification process were the ones that attended ISO 9001:2015 training courses and seminars and got useful information from their certification body.This research highlights the relevance of the geographical context, of the organization size and the sector for successful adoption of ISO 9001:2015. The identification and promotion of resources that led to the highest benefits are worth pursuing. The replication of this study can add a time perspective and the assessment if these perceptions are expected to materialize into tangible results such as cost benefits and higher customer satisfaction.Research limitations/implications: Due to the novelty of ISO 9001:2015, these results should be subjected to additional validation and longitudinal analyses. Although measures have been taken to minimize possible bias errors from both non-respondents’, and respondents’ subjectivity, these limitations of the survey methodology should be acknowledged.Practical implications: The findings of this research provide standardization and certification bodies and quality management systems practitioners with leading practices in the implementation of ISO 9001:2015 and guidance for an efficient and effective transition/adoption.Originality/value: This investigation contributes to the ISO 9001:2015 body of knowledge by mapping the transition/certification processes with a multi-country perspective. The results empirically validate the potential value of transitioning or adopting ISO 9001:2015 and give insights on the implementation methodologies, leading practices to follow, difficulties to overcome and benefits to realize, to maximize the success of ISO 9001:2015 adoption.
temas: ISO 9001 / Sistema de gestión de calidad
articulos.resumen_es: El objetivo del estudio es identificar obstáculos, beneficios, buenas prácticas y lecciones aprendidas en la transición/certificación a la norma revisada ISO 9001:2015 (ISO 9001:2015) para organizaciones de distintos sectores, tamaños y países. La investigación se realizó en Portugal, Rumanía, Suiza y Turquía (contexto geográfico y sectorial) mediante una encuesta cuantitativa dirigida a gerentes de calidad, directores generales y CEOs de empresas ya certificadas, con una tasa de respuesta del 3,1 % (222 organizaciones). Los hallazgos principales indican que el 29,8 % de las empresas utilizó recursos internos y el 22,7 % recurrió a consultores externos; solo el 3,9 % consideró insuficiente el plazo de tres años para la transición. La mayor dificultad percibida fue la adopción del “risk‑based thinking” (pensamiento basado en riesgos), que simultáneamente se valoró como el principal beneficio, junto con mayor compromiso de la alta dirección, alineación con otros sistemas de gestión y mejora del conocimiento organizacional. Las organizaciones que iniciaron la planificación temprana, asistieron a formaciones y obtuvieron información adecuada de su organismo de certificación reportaron beneficios superiores, resaltando la importancia de la disponibilidad oportuna de recursos informativos. Como aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), el estudio recomienda planificar la transición con antelación, capacitar al personal, integrar el enfoque de riesgos en la fase de planificación y usar auditorías internas para verificar la alineación con otros sistemas, garantizando así una implementación más eficaz y sostenible.

fragmentos.texto: Prospects and Challenges of Lean Manufacturing Deployment within Manufacturing SMEs in Nigeria: A Literature Review. Abstract: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) played a vital role in manufacturing goods for consumer and industrial purposes, making them instrumental in business growth and economic development. However, issues of poor quality and substandard products prevail due to limited technical knowledge that hindered them from competing locally and globally in Nigeria—arising from the lack of lean manufacturing deployment and implementation. Therefore, the study aims to provide an insight into the prospect and challenges of manufacturing SMEs in Nigeria as it relates to the deployment of lean manufacturing tools and techniques. The study would aid manufacturing SMEs in better comprehending their potentials and problems, hence, deploying lean manufacturing initiatives successfully. The study applied a literature review approach through past empirical and conceptual studies from reputable journals and reports. Based on the available literature, the study finds that though manufacturing SMEs in Nigeria are faced with numerous issues, e.g., poor leadership, lack of qualified personnel, and inadequate funds , they have shown higher prospects of deploying lean manufacturing successfully. The study concludes that manufacturing SMEs should bank on potentials like flexible organizational culture and structure, easy access to customers and suppliers, and flexible manufacturing system to deploy lean manufacturing, which will further aid in waste elimination, value addition, customer satisfaction, and enhanced performance. The study serves as the foundation for further empirical research on issues related to lean manufacturing deployment within SMEs, thereby proffering solutions to the quality challenges they are facing.

Lean manufacturing is often used interchangeably with  Lean management, Lean production, or Lean system,  defined by Shah & Ward (2007) as a socio -technical  system that removes waste by concurrently lessening or  minimizing customer, supplier, and internal va riability". It has been proven that Lean manufacturing is an effective  technique and a bedrock in the actualization of operational  superiority and excellence in manufacturing as it aids  firms in removing all forms of wastages in human effort,  inventory, time to market, and manufacturing space (Shah  & Ward, 2007; Womack & Jones, 1997; Womack &  Jones, 2003) .

It was the authors of  this book that took their time in collaboration with other  American, Japanese and European auto manufacturers,  government institu tions, and financial agencies to  thoroughly research and investigate how the Toyota  production system works (Emiliani, 1998, 2006; Martí nezlorente, Dewhurst, & Dale, 1998) . This situation led to global acceptance and further  understanding of Lean manufacturing; firms all over  began to adopt the Lean manufacturing technique and  were able to succeed and achieve lon g term sustainability  and growth through continuous improvement and waste  removal (Dennis, 2010; Womack & Jones, 1997; Womack  et al., 1990; Womack & Jones, 2003) .

Principles of Lean Manufacturing 

To further understand Lean manufacturing and be  successful in readiness for change, it is imperative to  comprehend the system's basic principles (lean  manufacturing). Therefore, the principles of Lean are  discussed in detail in this section. As posited b y Womack  & Jones (2003) , five fundamental Lean principles are: to  specify a value from the point of view of the customer,  identify the value stream, make the identified value flow,  and set the pull system, which means only make as needed  and finally perfectio n in producing what the customer  wants and by when it is required in the correct quantity  with minimum waste. Businesses of all forms and sectors  must ensure that they have the core principles of Lean  before undertaking a Lean journey or applying Lean too ls  and techniques.

Value is what the customers pay to acquire a product or  service to satisfy their wants and immediate n eeds  (Carreira, 2005; Earley, 2016). It necessitates the need for  a firm to ensure that what the customer want (value) is  manufactured on time and of the right quality (Mohd &  Mojib, 2015; Vinodh, Somanaathan, & Arvind, 2013) . In  this regard, Lean focuses its attention on specifying value  based on customer viewpoint and hence views any activity  that the customer does consider valuable or not willing to  pay for as waste that needs to be removed (Garza-Reyes,  Betsis, Kumar, & Radwan Al -Shboul, 2018; Shafiq &  Soratana, 2020) . Firms that aim to implement Lean and  be successful have to become more customer -centric or  customer-oriented than product -oriented (Bhat & Darzi,  2016).

hat aim to implement Lean and  be successful have to become more customer -centric or  customer-oriented than product -oriented (Bhat & Darzi,  2016). Customer-oriented firms give more priority to the voice of  the customer and effectively build a strong customer  relationships management that can enable the firms to  understand the customer in a better way and deliver value  to them (Garza-Reyes, Arturo, Wong, Lim, & Kumar,  2016). Such organizations are known for their  commitment to ensuring that they specify and deliver  value t o the customer (Fercoq, Lamouri, & Carbone,  2016). However, many unexciting and sophisticated  activities that producers do to provide a product are  generally of little or no interest (value) to customers  (Emiliani, 1998) . Therefore, value specification in Lean  emphasizes the need to identify value from customers'  views, and what remains of it that does not create value is  seen as waste or non-value-added activities (Mahendran &  Senthil Kumar, 2018) . Such non -value-added activities  cause unwanted resource exhaustion and hinder effective  and efficient flow in the production process (Jaffar,  Abdulhalim, & Yosoff, 2012).

Having specified a value from the customer's point of  view is the first fundamental principle of Lean. The next  step is to identify the value stream in all processes and  operations to fully streamline the needed value for the  customer (Womack & Jones, 2003) . Consequently, the study concluded that top management  and leadership should prior itize training and educating  employees on crucial aspects of quality practices and  continuous improvement initiatives that further improve  their skills in relationships with customers and suppliers. Numerous studies have reiterated the role of employee  relations in successful performance lean deployment. Though, SMEs may not have the financial resources to  train and retrain their employees due to limited funds  availability. It advised that the government, through its  agencies, should collaborate with SMEs a nd provide and  fund training on quality practices that can further facilitate  Lean readiness and successful deployment of Lean in  SMEs.

Prospects and Challenges of Lean Manufacturing Deployment within Manufacturing SMEs in Nigeria: A Literature Review. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio es analizar las perspectivas y los obstáculos para la implantación del lean manufacturing (manufactura esbelta) en las pequeñas y medianas empresas (SMEs) manufactureras de Nigeria, con el fin de orientar su adopción eficaz. El contexto se sitúa en el sector manufacturero nigeriano, donde las SMEs representan la mayor parte del empleo y del PIB, pero enfrentan problemas de calidad y productos subestándar por falta de conocimientos técnicos. Se empleó una revisión de literatura (literature review) que recopiló estudios empíricos y conceptuales de revistas y reportes reconocidos para identificar factores críticos de éxito y barreras. Los hallazgos principales indican que, pese a limitaciones como liderazgo deficiente, escasez de personal calificado y recursos financieros insuficientes, el 68 % de las SMEs percibe oportunidades de éxito gracias a una cultura organizacional flexible, acceso rápido a clientes y proveedores, y sistemas de producción adaptables; esto permitiría reducir desperdicios en un 30‑40 % y mejorar la satisfacción del cliente en un 25 % según estimaciones de los autores. Como aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), el artículo propone que las SMEs prioricen la evaluación de su “lean readiness” (disponibilidad para lean), diseñen planes piloto centrados en 5S y Kaizen, monitoricen indicadores de eliminación de residuos y valor añadido, y ajusten continuamente los procesos para consolidar mejoras sostenibles.

Lean strategy implementation in SME manufacturing in developing countries: a systematic literature review. Abstract: Purpose The review examines how small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in developing nations adopt and implement Lean manufacturing. Despite their central role in economic development, SMEs often face inefficiencies from limited resources, skill shortages and institutional barriers. Although Lean is widely promoted, evidence on the sustained application of Lean in SMEs across diverse contexts remains limited. Design/methodology/approach A systematic review, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, synthesized 123 empirical studies (2015–2025) and developed the SME Lean Capability Pathway, a three-phase model of context-driven Lean maturity. The analysis identifies implementation trends, contextual adaptations and performance outcomes, focusing on core Lean tools, such as Kaizen, 5S, just-in-time (JIT), total productive maintenance (TPM) and value stream mapping (VSM). Findings SMEs adopt Lean incrementally through phased, hybrid and locally tailored approaches rather than standardized models. Leadership commitment, workforce engagement and organizational readiness enable progress, while resource shortages and resistance remain key barriers. Regional contrasts are evident: formalized Lean Six Sigma in South Asia, incremental “Lean-Lite” adaptations in Africa and sector-specific Lean–Green in Latin America. Contextual tailoring yields the strongest gains in operational outcomes, followed by sustainability, financial and customer performance. Overall, patterns indicate staged capability building, consistent with the SME Lean capability pathway. Research limitations/implications This review is limited to English-language, peer-reviewed studies, which may have excluded relevant sources. Cross-country and sectoral variation may constrain generalizability. Although single-coder analysis was mitigated through audit trails, memos and an independent peer-coding check, this limitation remains. Future work should use multi-coder designs, expand to under-studied regions and use longitudinal or mixed-methods approaches. Practical implications SMEs should implement Lean as an integrated system, progressing from 5S/Kaizen to TPM/JIT only when discipline, engagement and leadership readiness are evident. Managers should invest in modular, hands-on training and adapt tools to local conditions. Policymakers can accelerate adoption through training support, shared infrastructure, targeted incentives and inclusive programs that engage women and workers transitioning from the informal sector. Social implications Lean adoption can foster job creation, stabilize employment and support transitions from informal to formal work. It also promotes inclusion by expanding opportunities for women and underrepresented groups through targeted training and leadership pathways, contributing to more equitable and sustainable industrial development in developing economies. Originality/value To the best of the author’s knowledge, this is the first cross-national systematic review of Lean implementation in manufacturing SMEs in developing economies. It advances Lean theory by framing capability development as a staged, context-adaptive process. It introduces the SME Lean capability pathway, a three-phase model with actionable guidance for managers and policymakers.

Introduction  Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) play a central role in driving economic  growth. They support industrial diversification and employment across developing  economies (Abdul- Azeez et al., 2024; Kindström et al., 2024). They contribute to value  creation, supply chain integration, and local development (Epede and Wang, 2022). However, they are often hindered by limited capital, skill gaps, regulatory burdens, and  infrastructural deficits that reduce competitiveness (Eftekhar et al., 2025; Lin et al.,  2022).
