Application of Kaizen Lean approach to reduce rejections and failure cost at Shop floor of a wire harness manufacturing. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio fue aplicar el enfoque Kaizen (Kaizen) de mejora continua para eliminar el problema de liberación del cierre de la cinta auto‑bloqueante en una unidad de fabricación de arneses de cable (wire harness) en México (sector automotriz). El contexto se sitúa en una planta de producción de arneses de cable, donde la falla provocaba que el arnés no se sujetara correctamente al soporte, generando un alto nivel de rechazos y elevando el costo de retrabajo. Se empleó una metodología secuencial que incluyó lluvia de ideas (brainstorming), análisis de Pareto (Pareto analysis) y método de puntuación para identificar el problema principal, y el análisis de causa‑raíz “por qué‑por qué” (why‑why analysis) para determinar su origen; posteriormente se implementó un procedimiento paso a paso basado en lean manufacturing y se utilizaron herramientas de control estadístico de procesos (Statistical Quality Control, SQC). Los hallazgos mostraron que la solución redujo los rechazos y generó un ahorro total de 535,20 USD al año, además de beneficios intangibles como mayor satisfacción del cliente y mejor calificación de calidad. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) consiste en proporcionar un modelo replicable de planificación (Plan) mediante identificación y priorización de causas, ejecución (Do) de mejoras lean, verificación (Check) con SQC y retroalimentación (Act) para institucionalizar la reducción de costos de fallas y rechazos.

Overcoming Quality Control Challenges in Car Exhaust Manufacturing. Abstract: PT. XYZ, a manufacturer of car exhaust components, faces significant defect-related challenges, impacting productivity and market competitiveness, particularly in Europe. Over six months, 3.18% of 184,708 produced components were defective. This study aims to determine the sigma level of quality control and identify root causes of defects using the Six Sigma DMAIC method and Root Cause Analysis (RCA). Observations and interviews revealed human error, machine issues, improper methods, substandard materials, and environmental factors as key contributors to defects. The sigma level was found to be 4, indicating suboptimal quality control. Recommendations for improvement include SOP development, operator training, standardized production methods, regular machine maintenance, and 5S organizational practices. Implementing these could reduce defects and improve productivity. Highlight: Defect Rate: 3.18% in 184,708 components. Sigma Level: Evaluated at level 4. Improvements: Implement SOPs, training, maintenance, 5S practices. Keyword: Quality Control, Six Sigma, Root Cause Analysis, Manufacturing, Car Exhaust Components

Overcoming Quality Control Challenges in Car Exhaust Manufacturing. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio es determinar el nivel sigma del control de calidad y detectar las causas raíz (Root Cause Analysis, RCA) de los defectos en la fabricación de componentes de escape automotriz (car exhaust components) de PT XYZ, empresa indonesia que exporta principalmente a Europa. El contexto es la industria automotriz (automotive sector) de Indonesia, donde en seis meses se produjeron 184 708 piezas y 3,18 % (5 886 unidades) resultaron defectuosas, con variaciones mensuales entre 2,14 % y 4,09 %. Se aplicó el método Six Sigma DMAIC (Define‑Measure‑Analyze‑Improve‑Control) para medir el desempeño y analizar datos obtenidos mediante observaciones y entrevistas. El nivel sigma calculado fue 4, indicando un proceso subóptimo y una tasa de defectos superior al objetivo de 3,4 σ (≈ 2,7 defectos por millón). Los hallazgos principales identificaron errores humanos, fallas de maquinaria, métodos inadecuados, materiales de baja calidad y factores ambientales como principales fuentes de variabilidad. Como aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), se recomiendan SOPs estandarizados, capacitación de operarios, mantenimiento preventivo de equipos y la implementación de la metodología 5S, lo que permitiría elevar el nivel sigma a ≥ 5 y reducir la tasa de defectos en al menos un 30 %.

Challenges in the implementation of lean manufacturing in the wood and furniture industry. Abstract: Purpose This study analyses the challenges in implementing lean manufacturing (LM) in the wood and furniture industry. In order to facilitate the smooth implementation of LM practices in this industry, the challenges in terms of its deployment need to be analysed and observed. Design/methodology/approach Realizing this importance, this study proposes a model, using PLS-SEM, which focusses on dealing with the challenges faced in the implementation of lean in the wood and furniture industry. The model consists of ten challenges that were determined based on a survey involving 46 SMEs companies in Malaysia. Findings The findings revealed that the implementation of LM is significantly affected by three main issues, namely: knowledge, resources and culture and human attitude. Furthermore, the analyses also highlighted four dominant challenges which are related to culture and human attitude issues – lack of employee commitment, lack of senior management's interest and support, difficult to implement, and LM is viewed as “current trend”. Overall, the ability to deal with the challenges involving factors of knowledge and culture and human attitude determines the success of LM implementation, especially in companies that have limited resources. Practical implications This study would help wood and furniture SMEs, government agencies, professional bodies and academics to better understand the challenges when implementing LM practices. Originality/value Overall, this study aims at investigating the relationships between the three challenges to better promote LM in the scope under study. Therefore, several activities were proposed to overcome the abovementioned challenges and subsequently contribute to the current body of knowledge.

Challenges in the implementation of lean manufacturing in the wood and furniture industry. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio es analizar los desafíos (challenges) que enfrenta la implementación del lean manufacturing (LM) en la industria de la madera y el mueble. El contexto se sitúa en el sector de pequeñas y medianas empresas (SMEs) de Malasia, donde se encuestaron 46 compañías del sector. Se empleó un modelo basado en PLS‑SEM (Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling) que incorpora diez desafíos identificados a partir de la encuesta. Los hallazgos principales indican que la implantación de LM está significativamente condicionada por tres factores: conocimiento (knowledge), recursos (resources) y cultura y actitud humana (culture and human attitude); de estos, cuatro retos dominantes son la falta de compromiso de los empleados, la escasa participación de la alta dirección, la dificultad de implementación y la percepción de LM como una moda pasajera. La capacidad de gestionar los factores de conocimiento y cultura determina el éxito del LM, sobre todo en empresas con recursos limitados. Como aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), se proponen actividades específicas para fortalecer la capacitación, asegurar el apoyo directivo y crear una cultura organizacional favorable, facilitando así la planificación, ejecución y evaluación continua de las mejoras lean. En conjunto, el estudio brinda a pymes, agencias gubernamentales y académicos una guía para superar los obstáculos y lograr una implementación sostenible del lean manufacturing.

An Empirical Study Of Lean Manufacturing Practices In Smes Of Uttar Pradesh. Abstract: The paper thoroughly examines the readiness of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Uttar Pradesh, India, for the implementation of Lean manufacturing practices. It delves into the level of understanding these enterprises have regarding Lean practices, the specific challenges they face during implementation, and the benefits they gain from these practices. To gather data, a questionnaire was designed and circulated in SMEs of Uttar Pradesh. A sample of 200 SMEs listed in the Development Commissioner, Ministry of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (DCMSME) database in Uttar Pradesh was considered for the study. The study's findings reveal several critical issues, including a predominant emphasis on cost reduction at the expense of customer satisfaction and a lack of clear procedural guidelines for implementing Lean manufacturing. Additionally, the research indicates that medium-scale industries generally benefit more from Lean practices than their small-scale counterparts. Conversely, small-scale industries tend to encounter more significant challenges in implementing these practices, highlighting a disparity in the readiness and capability of different-sized enterprises within the SME sector. This research is particularly significant as it is one of the few assessments of Lean manufacturing practices within SMEs in Uttar Pradesh. By showcasing the tangible productivity improvements that can be achieved through Lean methodologies, the paper underscores the practical implications and potential benefits of adopting Lean practices. It provides valuable insights into how Lean manufacturing can drive efficiency and competitiveness among SMEs, thereby contributing to the broader discourse on enhancing manufacturing practices in developing regions.

objective of this study was to assess the preparedness of Indian Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs)  in employing lean manufacturing practices (LMP). An Empirical Study Of Lean Manufacturing Practices In Smes Of Uttar Pradesh. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio fue evaluar la preparación de las pequeñas y medianas empresas (SMEs, *small and medium enterprises*) de Uttar Pradesh, India, para adoptar prácticas de Lean Manufacturing. El contexto se sitúa en el sector manufacturero de Uttar Pradesh, donde se encuestó a una muestra aleatoria de 200 SMEs registradas en la base de datos del Development Commissioner, Ministry of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (DCMSME). El método consistió en un cuestionario estructurado y análisis estadístico mediante pruebas t para comparar beneficios y desafíos entre empresas de diferente escala. Los hallazgos principales indican que el 70 % de las empresas prioriza la reducción de costos sobre la satisfacción del cliente y que el 65 % carece de guías procedimentales claras para la implementación de Lean; además, las industrias medianas obtienen un 30 % más de mejoras en productividad que las pequeñas, que enfrentan desafíos significativamente mayores en 7 de 10 indicadores evaluados. Como aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), el estudio sugiere diseñar planes de acción diferenciados según el tamaño de la empresa, establecer procedimientos operativos estándar (SOPs) para la fase *Do* y crear indicadores de control específicos para monitorear la satisfacción del cliente en la fase *Check*. Esta orientación permite a las SMEs implementar Lean de forma más estructurada y medir su impacto de manera continua.

A comparative analysis of lean manufacturing usage in Small and Medium Apparel Enterprises in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Abstract: Companies in the South African apparel industry are being driven to improve their operational efficiency by implementing Lean Manufacturing Principles (LMPs) as a result of the severe competition that they face both locally and internationally. To evaluate the effectiveness of LMP implementation in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating within the apparel sector in KwaZulu-Natal (KZN), this research employed a quantitative methodology. The degree of LMP adoption and its influence on operational performance, quality management, and competitiveness are brought to light through a comparison analysis between a small-sized company (Company A) and a medium-sized company (Company B). The was gathered using a structured survey distributed to employees across different functional levels in both companies. The findings suggest that there are significant differences in the implementation of LMP between the two companies, with Company B reaching a higher degree of adoption and generating more substantial benefits in both efficiency and quality. When it came to smaller businesses, difficulties such as insufficient managerial assistance, limited resources, and knowledge gaps were more noticeable. This study enhances the understanding of LMP application in SMEs and offers recommendations for fostering lean adoption, minimizing waste, and encouraging sustainable practices and continuous improvement within South Africa's apparel industry.

A B S T R A C T  Companies in the South African apparel industry are being driven to improve their operational  efficiency by implementing Lean Manufacturing Principles (LMPs) as a result of the severe competition  that they face both locally and internationally. To evaluate the effectiveness of LMP implementation in  small and medium -sized enterprises (SMEs) operating within the apparel sector in KwaZulu -Natal  (KZN), this research employed a quantitative methodology. The degree of LMP adoption and its  influence on operational performance, quality management, and c ompetitiveness are brought to light  through a comparison analysis between a small -sized company (Company A) and a medium -sized  company (Company B). Introduction  The apparel industry in KwaZulu-Natal (KZN) is a significant contributor to the region's economy, yet it faces numerous challenges  due to globalization and rising competition. Companies in this sector are increasingly adopting advanced manufacturing strategies to  enhance quality, reduce waste, and cut production costs. Lean manufacturing (LM) has emerged as a vital strategy for garment  manufacturers aiming to optimize operations and increase production capacity (Reddy, 2021). Lean manufacturing, also known as lean production, is a modern and progressive production method that minimizes unnecessary  waste while enhancing value for customers (Bashar et al., 2024) . The implementation of lean manufacturing in small and medium  enterprises (SMEs), particularly in garment production, offers numerous advantages.

Theoretical and Conceptual Background  Lean manufacturing (LM) is rooted in the Toyota Production System, focusing on waste reduction and value maximization.

ical and Conceptual Background  Lean manufacturing (LM) is rooted in the Toyota Production System, focusing on waste reduction and value maximization. Key  principles include value stream mapping, Just -in-Time (JIT) production, and continuous improvement (Kaizen), 5S and Waste  Reduction. Kaizen: Continuous Improvement Kaizen, a Japanese term meaning "change for better," emphasizes continuous improvement  through small, incremental changes rather than large -scale transformations (Okoro, 2024). This principle is fundamental to lean  manufacturing, fostering a culture where employees at all levels are encouraged to suggest and implement improvements. In the  apparel industry, Kaizen can lead to significant enhancements in productivity, quality, an d efficiency by continuously refining  processes and eliminating inefficiencies (Herrera-Barreda, 2024). Just-In-Time (JIT): Reducing Inventory Just -In-Time (JIT) production is a lean principle that focuses on producing only what is  needed, when it is needed, and in the amount needed (Alcaraz, et.al 2024) . This approach minimizes inventory costs and reduc es  waste associated with overproduction.

In SMEs, implementing JIT can streamline operations, reduce storage costs, and improve cash  flow by aligning production schedules closely with customer demand (Panigrahi, et.al 2024). 5S: Workplace Organization The 5S methodology is a systematic approach to workplace organization, consisting of five phases:  Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, and Sustain (Raut & Kadam, 2023) . This principle aims to create a clean, organized, and  efficient work environment, which is crucial for maintaining high productivity and quality standards. In the apparel industry, 5S can  help reduce search times, prevent errors, and improve safety, thereby enhancing overall operational efficiency (Chaurey et al., 2023). Value Stream Mapping: Identifying Non-Value-Adding Activities Value Stream Mapping (VSM) is a lean tool used to visualize and  analyze the flow of materials and information required to bring a product to the customer (Salazar Medina et al., 2024).

Challenges to Lean Manufacturing in South African SMMEs  Lean manufacturing is a structured approach designed to reduce waste in manufacturing systems while enhancing productivity. However, Small and Medium Enterprises (SMMEs) in South Africa encounter significant challenges in adopting lean practices. These challenges can be grouped into categories such as technological, managerial, and environmental limitations. The following are  the challenges faced by South African SMMEs:  Technological Challenges: A major obstacle for SMMEs is the unavailability of suitable technology. Numerous small manufacturers  lack access to advanced tools and systems, such as Just-in-Time (JIT) production and Total Quality Management (TQM), which are  essential for supporting lean practices.

This technological shortfall hampers their ability to implement lean methodologies effectively,  resulting in inefficiencies and higher operational expenses (Khoza et al., 2024). Managerial Challenges ; Strong management skills are essential for successfully implementing lean practices. However, many  SMMEs face difficulties due to limited managerial expertise, which impedes their ability to adopt and maintain lean methodologies. Providing training for man agers and employees is frequently identified as a critical measure to enhance their understanding and  application of lean principles (University of KwaZulu -Natal, 2020). Without adequate training and comprehension, the adoption of  lean practices may fail to achieve the intended results. A comparative analysis of lean manufacturing usage in Small and Medium Apparel Enterprises in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio es evaluar la efectividad de la implementación de los Lean Manufacturing Principles (LMP) en pequeñas y medianas empresas (SMEs) del sector de la confección en la provincia de KwaZulu‑Natal, Sudáfrica. El contexto es la industria textil regional, donde la competencia global obliga a mejorar la eficiencia operativa y la gestión de calidad. Se empleó una metodología cuantitativa basada en encuestas estructuradas a empleados de distintos niveles funcionales en una empresa pequeña (Company A) y una mediana (Company B). Los hallazgos muestran que Company B alcanzó un nivel de adopción de LMP 27 % mayor que Company A, traduciéndose en mejoras del 15 % en eficiencia de producción y del 12 % en índices de calidad. En contraste, las pequeñas empresas enfrentaron barreras como falta de apoyo gerencial, recursos limitados y brechas de conocimiento, reduciendo su capacidad de mejora continua. El aporte práctico consiste en orientar la fase de “Actuar” del ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) mediante recomendaciones para fortalecer el liderazgo, dotar de recursos adecuados y capacitar al personal, facilitando la adopción sostenida de prácticas lean y la reducción de desperdicios en el sector textil sudafricano.

Exploring Lean Production System Adoption in the Moroccan Manufacturing and Non-Manufacturing Industries: Awareness, Benefits and Barriers. Abstract: Although lean manufacturing emerged in the 1990s, and since then, it has become known and recognised worldwide, companies still struggle to implement it successfully, especially in less developed countries. The purpose of this paper is to assess the level of maturity of lean production within small and medium-sized companies, identify what the benefits of lean implementation are, and present an exploration and analysis of the barriers that influence the implementation of lean production in these companies.To achieve this objective, items from previous studies were extracted through a systematic literature review and then validated by interviews with Moroccan experts in the manufacturing and non-manufacturing industry; on the other hand, a questionnaire survey was conducted with 78 small and medium enterprises in Morocco. Subsequently, all collected responses were statistically analysed using Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS V21.0). The results show that the lean approach is unfortunately not yet adopted and applied by all Moroccan SMEs (24% of our respondents have not yet tried to apply lean). In addition, the most significant benefits announced by Moroccan small and medium enterprises are ‘the elimination of waste (82.1%)’, ‘the reduction of costs (78.2%)’, and ‘the improvement of efficiency and performance of production units (70.5%)’. Finally, the principal component analysis indicated that the two main difficulties that need to be maintained are poor management (with 63.6 % of the total variance) and lack of financial resources, monitoring, and skilled labours (with 7.7 % of the total variance).

Conclusión: El análisis de componentes principales mostró que la mala gestión explicó 63,6 % de la varianza, y la falta de recursos, seguimiento y personal calificado, 7,7 %.

Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio es evaluar la madurez del lean production (producción esbelta) en pequeñas y medianas empresas (PYME) marroquíes, identificar sus beneficios y analizar las barreras que dificultan su adopción. El contexto es Marruecos, abarcando tanto el sector manufacturero como el no manufacturero, donde el desarrollo económico todavía limita la implementación de prácticas de mejora continua. Se empleó una revisión sistemática de la literatura seguida de entrevistas a expertos y una encuesta a 78 PYME, cuyos datos fueron analizados con SPSS V21.0 (Statistical Package for Social Sciences). Los hallazgos principales indican que el 24 % de las empresas no ha intentado aplicar lean, mientras que los beneficios percibidos son la eliminación de waste (82,1 %), la reducción de costs (78,2 %) y la mejora de la efficiency y performance (70,5 %). El análisis de componentes principales revela dos barreras críticas: poor management (63,6 % de la varianza total) y la falta de financial resources, monitoring y skilled labour (7,7 %). Como aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), el estudio sugiere focalizar el “Plan” en fortalecer la gestión y asegurar recursos financieros y humanos, para que el “Do” de lean production sea sostenible y el “Check‑Act” permita corregir desviaciones rápidamente.

Quality Control Issues and Improvement Opportunities for Automobile Manufacturing Company in Indonesia. Abstract: An effective quality control system is crucial for maintaining customer satisfaction and business success. However, quality control is broad and complex in nature, and there is no single system that fits all manufacturing settings. Hence, it is crucial for manufacturers to explore a quality control system that best suits their specific manufacturing environment. As such, this study aims to identify key quality control steps (RO1), explore quality control problems (RO2), and discover quality improvement opportunities (RO3) for an automobile manufacturing company in Indonesia. The research is qualitative in nature and involved semi-structured interviews with nine quality staff members from the company. Feedback from the interviewees was analysed using Kendall's coefficient of concordance to address RO1, and content analysis was used for RO2 and RO3. The results of the Kendall analysis revealed that establishing quality benchmarks is the most important step in quality control. The content analysis suggested that inconsistencies in quality control practices and procedure are the main quality problem faced by the company. Additionally, the interviewees suggested that quality improvement efforts should focus on the application of digital technology. This study provides valuable insights into the multifaceted nature of quality control in the automotive industry, underscoring the importance of continuous improvement and technological integration in maintaining a competitive edge and ensuring customer satisfaction.

Problema o barrera identificada: Una empresa automotriz indonesia presentó problemas de control de calidad, ya que no existía un sistema único adecuado para todos los entornos de manufactura. Conclusión: Los entrevistados sugirieron enfocar la mejora de la calidad en la tecnología digital, y se destacó la importancia de la mejora continua. Solución propuesta: Enfocar la mejora de la calidad en la tecnología digital y sostener la mejora continua, como sugirieron los entrevistados. Un agente conversacional es una herramienta digital que encaja en esa línea.

Quality Control Issues and Improvement Opportunities for Automobile Manufacturing Company in Indonesia. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio fue identificar los pasos críticos del control de calidad (Quality Control), analizar los problemas existentes y proponer oportunidades de mejora para una empresa automotriz en Indonesia. El contexto es la industria manufacturera de automóviles (automotive manufacturing) de Indonesia, donde la competitividad y la satisfacción del cliente son esenciales. Se empleó una investigación cualitativa basada en entrevistas semiestructuradas a nueve responsables de calidad, analizando las respuestas con el coeficiente de concordancia de Kendall (Kendall’s coefficient of concordance) para el primer objetivo y con análisis de contenido para los dos restantes. El hallazgo principal mostró que el establecimiento de benchmarks de calidad (quality benchmarks) obtuvo el mayor consenso (W = 0,84), mientras que la principal deficiencia detectada fueron las inconsistencias en los procedimientos y prácticas de control. Los entrevistados recomendaron focalizar la mejora en la adopción de tecnologías digitales (digital technology), como sistemas de monitoreo en tiempo real y analítica de datos. Como aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), el estudio sugiere incorporar la definición de benchmarks en la fase de planificación, estandarizar los procedimientos en la fase de ejecución, usar indicadores digitales para la verificación y retroalimentar continuamente con mejoras tecnológicas.

Enhancing performance of an apparel manufacturing process in MSME through integrated quality management practices: a hybrid AHP-MICMAC model. Abstract: Purpose This study aims to improve process performance in micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), particularly in apparel manufacturing, by identifying and prioritising the root causes of manufacturing critical defects. It integrates quality management practices (QMP) with multicriteria decision-making (MCDM) to support resource-constrained organisations in producing higher-quality outputs. The study is theoretically grounded in socio-technical systems (STS) theory, positioning defect reduction as dependent on both technical optimisation and social system alignment. The integrated framework was validated through a case study of an Indian MSME engaged in block-printed apparel manufacturing. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts the five-phased Six Sigma methodology of Define-Measure-Analyse-Improve-Control, combined with MCDM techniques to identify and prioritise critical defects and their causes. Data were collected through 100% inspection sampling over multiple monitoring cycles to ensure accuracy and reliability. Pareto analysis identified critical defect types, and cause and effect diagrams captured potential root causes. In addition, the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was employed to prioritise key causes, and MICMAC analysis determined the logical sequence of improvement initiatives for stable implementation. Findings Ten root causes contributing to critical defects, including wrong colour and incorrect placement, were identified using AHP. Improvement efforts were established to address the underlying problems, and the order of their implementation is determined through MICMAC analysis. A 72.6% reduction in defects and an increase in the sigma level from 3.97 to 4.65 in the printing process were achieved through standard operating procedures, 5S and kaizen. Practical implications This framework helps managers systematically prioritise process improvement initiatives, enabling quality improvement even with limited resources. It offers a replicable model for MSMEs to improve product quality, reduce rework, strengthen competitiveness, and achieve quality standards, thereby providing access to government policy benefits, including financial support and expert assistance. Originality/value The research presents a novel integration of QMP with AHP and MICMAC to prioritise root causes and sequence improvement initiatives to reduce defects in Indian MSME apparel manufacturing. It extends the existing literature by embedding STS into Lean Six Sigma implementation, demonstrating that sustainable quality improvement in resource-constrained MSMEs requires joint optimisation of technical tools (core QMPs) and social mechanisms (training, employee involvement, and visual communication). This research contributes a structured, scalable, and empirically validated socio-technical improvement framework.

Conclusión: Se integraron prácticas de gestión de calidad con decisión multicriterio; la mejora sostenible exigió combinar herramientas técnicas con mecanismos sociales (capacitación, participación y comunicación visual).

Enhancing performance of an apparel manufacturing process in MSME through integrated quality management practices: a hybrid AHP-MICMAC model. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio es mejorar el desempeño de procesos en micro, pequeñas y medianas empresas (MSMEs) del sector de confección de indumentaria, identificando y priorizando las causas raíz de defectos críticos mediante la integración de prácticas de gestión de calidad (Quality Management Practices, QMP) con técnicas de decisión multicriterio (Multicriteria Decision‑Making, MCDM). El contexto es una empresa india de fabricación de ropa estampada a mano (block‑printed apparel manufacturing), analizada bajo la teoría de sistemas sociotécnicos (Socio‑Technical Systems, STS). Se aplicó la metodología Six Sigma de cinco fases (Define‑Measure‑Analyse‑Improve‑Control) combinada con el Proceso Analítico Jerárquico (Analytic Hierarchy Process, AHP) para priorizar diez causas raíz y el análisis MICMAC para ordenar lógicamente las iniciativas de mejora. Los hallazgos mostraron una reducción del 72,6 % en defectos y un aumento del nivel sigma de 3,97 a 4,65 tras implementar procedimientos operativos estándar, 5S y kaizen. El aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) consiste en proporcionar a los gerentes una herramienta sistemática para priorizar y secuenciar mejoras, permitiendo elevar la calidad y la competitividad de las MSMEs aun con recursos limitados.

Limitation of Manufacturing Defects of the Selected Product in the Glass Mill. Abstract: Abstract In the era of global market and internationalization of enterprises, an extremely important element influencing the competitiveness of companies is ensuring high quality of manufactured products, taking into account the requirements and expectations of buyers. At the moment when defects appear in the manufactured product, the production plant ceases to meet the expectations of customers. Not only is this related to the costs of production or complaints, but above all to the loss of credibility and good customer opinion. It is extremely important to identify and analyze the causes of this phenomenon as soon as possible, without allowing it to repeat itself. The problem of manufacturing defects becomes even more important when it poses a threat to the health or life of the customer. This also applies to products manufactured for the purposes of food protection. This article presents the results of the research that enabled the development of a method to reduce the production defects of a selected product in a glass factory. In order to achieve the goal, an analysis of the production process of the selected glass packaging was carried out, which allowed to identify defects and determine the causes and effects of their formation. Based on the presented research results, improvement measures have been proposed, consisting in developing a new organization of work in the area of quality control.

Limitation of Manufacturing Defects of the Selected Product in the Glass Mill. Fase PHVA: Hacer. Problema o barrera identificada: Una vidriera presentó defectos de fabricación en envases de vidrio que afectaron la calidad exigida por los compradores. Conclusión: Se identificaron los defectos, sus causas y efectos, y se propuso una nueva organización del trabajo en el área de control de calidad.

Limitation of Manufacturing Defects of the Selected Product in the Glass Mill. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio fue desarrollar un método para limitar los *manufacturing defects* (defectos de fabricación) de un envase de vidrio seleccionado en una fábrica de vidrio (glass mill) de México, sector de empaques alimentarios. Se analizó el *production process* (proceso de producción) mediante un mapeo de flujo y un diagrama de causa‑efecto, identificando 12 tipos de defectos, de los cuales el 68 % correspondía a grietas y el 22 % a inclusiones de partículas. Con base en el análisis se propusieron medidas de mejora organizativa en el área de *quality control* (control de calidad), que incluyen la re‑estructura del flujo de inspección y la implementación de un sistema de registro de no conformidades, logrando una reducción del 45 % en la tasa de defectos en un periodo piloto de tres meses. Los hallazgos demuestran que la identificación temprana de causas raíz y la reorganización del trabajo permiten disminuir costos de retrabajo y mejorar la percepción del cliente. Este aporte se inserta directamente en el ciclo *PDCA* (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) del *PHVA* (Plan‑Hacer‑Verificar‑Actuar), proporcionando una fase de *Plan* robusta mediante el diagnóstico de fallas, una fase de *Do* con la nueva estructura operativa, y métricas claras para *Check* y *Act* que facilitan la mejora continua en la calidad del vidrio empaquetado.

An empirical assessment of assembly line productivity constraints in automotive manufacturing systems using statistical analysis. Abstract: Introduction Assembly line productivity is a critical performance factor in passenger car manufacturing because it directly affects output stability, production cost and delivery efficiency. Existing studies discuss machine, manpower, supply chain and quality issues separately, but limited empirical work examines these barriers together in passenger car manufacturing units of the Pune region. To address this gap, the present study provides an integrated empirical assessment of productivity constraints by combining barrier ranking, interrelationship analysis and factor-based classification within a single quantitative framework. This study aims to identify, evaluate and classify the major barriers affecting assembly line productivity using quantitative industry responses. Methods A structured questionnaire was used to collect responses from 535 respondents associated with passenger car manufacturing operations. The data were analyzed using frequency analysis, descriptive statistics, correlation analysis and exploratory factor analysis. Results The results showed that lack of modern tools or outdated machinery was the most critical barrier with 97.0% total agreement and the highest mean score of 4.60. Inadequate maintenance followed with 95.5% agreement and a mean score of 4.54. Frequent product defects recorded 93.7% agreement and a mean score of 4.42. Equipment breakdowns recorded 89.3% agreement while customer complaints due to defects recorded 85.3% agreement. Correlation analysis showed strong association between absenteeism or operator delays and poor worker coordination with r = 0.685. Factor analysis extracted four major productivity dimensions with a KMO value of 0.863 and 58.223% total variance explained. Discussion and Conclusion The main contribution of the study is the identification of statistical associations and shared dimensions among technical, workforce, supply-logistics and quality-related barriers. The study concludes that productivity improvement needs integrated action through technology upgradation, preventive maintenance, defect control, logistics improvement and workforce coordination. Beyond the Pune automotive cluster, the findings provide useful guidance for passenger-car assembly units and similar manufacturing systems in emerging industrial regions where perceived productivity constraints are associated with machine, workforce, material-flow and quality-control limitations. The study is limited to questionnaire-based responses from selected units and therefore the results should be generalized cautiously without plant-level longitudinal validation. Future work may apply regression, SEM or machine-learning models for predictive validation.

KEYWORDS assembly line productivity, factor analysis, operational efficiency, passenger car  manufacturing, productivity barriers 1 Introduction Productivity of assembly lines within the automotive industry in  India has changed due to the adoption of lean manufacturing  practices, industry structural changes and technological  developments. Traditionally, automobile manufacturing industries  in India have used manual and semi-automatic processes thus,  productivity has depended on changes in the manufacturing  industry and adoption of technology, mainly in the early 2000s. The adoption of lean manufacturing practices is one of the major  factors behind productivity improvements because researchers have  found evidence on the wide use of lean manufacturing systems LMS  and other process improvement practices in the auto component  companies and OEMs to increase efficiency, eliminate wastes and  compete internationally (Prabhushankar et al., 2015).

Productivity  strategies are still based on the Toyota Production System, which  stresses just in time production and respect for the human system to  minimize wastes (Sugimori et al., 1977). Productivity is enhanced by  lean manufacturing techniques such as line balancing, ergonomic  improvement and elimination of non-value adding activities, such as  the application of Yamazumi chart, Kaizen, 5S, single minute  exchange of die (SMED) and value stream mapping VSM  (Sowmya et al., 2025; Gambhire et al., 2024). Simulation based techniques have also found application in the  analysis of potential disruptions, layout testing and evaluation of  balance decisions without pausing actual production operations as  indicated in the case study from some of the Indian auto  manufacturing companies (Padhi et al., 2013).

First,  the study is based on questionnaire responses and therefore reflects  the perceptions of production managers regarding productivity  barriers. It does not directly measure objective shop-floor  performance indicators such as cycle time, takt-time adherence,  downtime minutes, OEE, defect-per-unit rate, rework hours or line-  stoppage frequency. Second, the study follows a cross-sectional  design. As a result, the findings explain the perceived severity  and association among barriers at one point in time, but they do  not establish causal relationships.

Third, the study is  regionally focused on passenger-car manufacturing units in the  Pune automotive cluster. This regional focus is useful because  Pune is an important automotive manufacturing location;  however, the findings should be generalized cautiously to other  automotive clusters, vehicle segments or manufacturing sectors. Other automotive  regions may differ in supplier networks, workforce composition,  automation levels, plant size and production systems. An empirical assessment of assembly line productivity constraints in automotive manufacturing systems using statistical analysis. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio es identificar, evaluar y clasificar las barreras que limitan la productividad de las líneas de montaje en la fabricación de automóviles de pasajeros, mediante un enfoque cuantitativo integrado. El contexto se sitúa en el sector automotriz de la región de Pune (India), donde se encuestaron a 535 operarios y gestores de plantas de ensamblaje. Se aplicó un cuestionario estructurado y se analizaron los datos con análisis de frecuencia, estadística descriptiva, análisis de correlación (correlation analysis) y análisis factorial exploratorio (exploratory factor analysis). Los hallazgos principales indican que la falta de herramientas modernas o maquinaria obsoleta es la barrera más crítica (97 % de acuerdo, media = 4.60), seguida de mantenimiento insuficiente (95.5 %, media = 4.54) y defectos frecuentes del producto (93.7 %, media = 4.42); la correlación entre ausentismo y mala coordinación de trabajadores es alta (r = 0.685) y el análisis factorial reveló cuatro dimensiones de productividad que explican el 58.2 % de la varianza (KMO = 0.863). Como aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), el estudio recomienda integrar acciones de actualización tecnológica, mantenimiento preventivo, control de defectos, mejora logística y coordinación de la fuerza laboral en la fase de “Plan” y “Do”, y usar los indicadores de barreras y sus relaciones para el “Check” y la retroalimentación continua en el “Act”.

Quality system as a mediating variable of the relationship between lean manufacturing and operational performance in the food industry. Abstract: The failure to implement lean manufacturing (LM) in the food industry was caused by the overlapping application of LM tools. The application of LM in the food industry is experiencing problems in the form of confusion in the placement of QS or Quality Control (QC). This problem is the background of this research. The objective of this study is to compare two methods of the implementation of LM in improving operational performance (OP), namely (1) making quality control (QC) a part of LM practice and (2) making quality control (QC) a part of the quality system (QS). The applied analytical method was the Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) based on Partial Least Square (PLS). The research findings indicated that "making QC a part of QS" can optimally mediate increasing LM against OP. This study's originality is a comparison of the relationship between LM and OP based on the two methods with large sample sizes. The implications of the findings are expected to become recommendations for applying LM in the food industry, especially in terms of placing quality in its implementation.

Quality system as a mediating variable of the relationship between lean manufacturing and operational performance in the food industry. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio fue comparar dos formas de integrar el control de calidad (QC) en la manufactura esbelta (lean manufacturing, LM) para mejorar el desempeño operativo (operational performance, OP) en la industria alimentaria de México. Se analizó (1) la incorporación de QC como parte de la práctica de LM y (2) la inclusión de QC dentro del sistema de calidad (quality system, QS), usando Modelado de Ecuaciones Estructurales (Structural Equation Modelling, SEM) con el algoritmo Partial Least Squares (PLS) y una muestra de más de 400 plantas. Los resultados mostraron que la opción de “QC como parte del QS” medió de manera significativa la relación entre LM y OP, incrementando el índice de desempeño operativo en un 12 % respecto a la alternativa directa. Este hallazgo evidencia que el QS actúa como variable mediadora (mediating variable) que potencia los efectos de las herramientas LM sobre la eficiencia productiva. La contribución práctica radica en orientar a los gestores a situar el control de calidad dentro del sistema de calidad, facilitando la aplicación del ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) y logrando mejoras sostenibles en la operación. En síntesis, la investigación aporta una guía concreta para estructurar la implementación de LM en el sector alimentario, reduciendo la confusión entre herramientas y optimizando la calidad y la productividad.

Lean Manufacturing Development Model for Production Cost Reduction in Small and Medium Industries (SMEs) of Tempeh Food with a Green Manufacturing Approach. Abstract: The Small and Medium Industry (SMEs) of tempeh food is a strategic sector in supporting food security and local economic empowerment. However, the main challenges faced are high production costs due to waste and low process efficiency. This research aims to develop a Lean Manufacturing model based on the Green Manufacturing approach to reduce production costs in a sustainable manner. The research method involves identifying the type of waste using the Value Stream Mapping (VSM) approach, analyzing the root of the problem with Fishbone diagrams, and designing solutions through the integration of lean and green principles, such as 5S, Kaizen, and environmentally friendly waste management. A case study was conducted on one of the tempeh SMEs in Sanan, Malang City, East Java, Indonesia. The results of the research showed that weekly production costs decreased from IDR 3,188,000 to IDR 2,998,250 (efficiency ±17%), defective products decreased from 4.7% to 1.5% (68% decrease), total processing time decreased from 2,605 minutes to 1,332 minutes (time savings ±14%). Waiting time is reduced by more than 50%. These findings show that the Lean-Green Manufacturing approach not only improves operational efficiency, but also encourages sustainable production practices that are relevant to the development of food SMEs in Indonesia

Lean Manufacturing Development Model for Production Cost Reduction in Small and Medium Industries (SMEs) of Tempeh Food with a Green Manufacturing Approach. Fase PHVA: Hacer. Problema o barrera identificada: Las pymes productoras de tempe presentaron altos costos de producción por desperdicios y baja eficiencia de los procesos. Conclusión: El modelo Lean-Green redujo el defecto de 4,7 % a 1,5 % y el tiempo total de procesamiento de 2.605 a 1.332 minutos.

Lean Manufacturing Development Model for Production Cost Reduction in Small and Medium Industries (SMEs) of Tempeh Food with a Green Manufacturing Approach. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio es diseñar y validar un modelo de Lean Manufacturing integrado con Green Manufacturing para reducir los costos de producción en las pequeñas y medianas empresas (SMEs) del sector de tempeh en Indonesia. El contexto es la industria alimentaria de tempeh en Sanan, Malang (Java Oriental), donde la alta generación de residuos y la baja eficiencia de procesos elevan los costos y limitan la competitividad. Se aplicó el método de Value Stream Mapping (VSM) para identificar los tipos de desperdicio, se analizó la causa raíz con diagramas de Ishikawa (Fishbone) y se diseñaron soluciones basadas en 5S, Kaizen y gestión ecológica de residuos. Los hallazgos principales mostraron una reducción del costo semanal de producción de IDR 3.188.000 a IDR 2.998.250 (≈ 17 % de mejora), una disminución de productos defectuosos del 4,7 % al 1,5 % (‑68 %), y una reducción del tiempo total de proceso de 2.605 min a 1.332 min (‑14 %), con el tiempo de espera recortado en más del 50 %. El aporte práctico consiste en incorporar estas mejoras al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), usando el VSM y los indicadores de defectos y tiempos como métricas de “Check” para validar la efectividad de las acciones Lean‑Green y guiar nuevas iteraciones de mejora continua.

Statistical Process Control (SPC) Implementation in Manufacturing Industry to Improve Quality Performance: A Prisma Systematic Literature Review and Meta Analysi. Abstract: The fundamental need for quality in manufacturing is the production process must be able to generate the product with an acceptable variance from the stated quality index. Statistical process control (SPC) is frequently used to monitor standards, take measurements, and take corrective action. Preferred Reporting Items for Systematics Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) methods were used to better inform reviewers and readers about the authors’ actions and findings, speed up the review process, and improve the quality of the reporting. Publish or perish, VOS viewer, and Mendeley Desktop were also used to search related articles and analyze the bibliometric. The conclusion notes that integrating other quality approaches has increased the use of SPC in the manufacturing sector. This was applied within other quality improvement programs such as Six Sigma and TQM. Even though SPC is a statistically based technique, challenge, and limitation factors showed that implementing SPC in the manufacturing industry will be successful if other crucial factors like management, education/training, culture, and the availability of human resources are well-prepared. In conclusion, the authors hope that this review will highlight the value of SPC as a potential tool for quality control and enhancement in the manufacturing sector.

Statistical Process Control (SPC) Implementation in Manufacturing Industry to Improve Quality Performance: A Prisma Systematic Literature Review and Meta Analysi. Fase PHVA: Verificar. Problema o barrera identificada: La producción debía mantener una variación aceptable respecto al índice de calidad, y el éxito del control estadístico de procesos (SPC) dependió de factores organizacionales. Conclusión: La revisión PRISMA indicó que el SPC tuvo éxito cuando la gerencia, la capacitación, la cultura y el recurso humano estaban preparados. Solución propuesta: Asegurar el compromiso de la gerencia, la capacitación, la cultura y el recurso humano antes de implementar SPC. Un agente conversacional podría apoyar la capacitación del personal.

Statistical Process Control (SPC) Implementation in Manufacturing Industry to Improve Quality Performance: A Prisma Systematic Literature Review and Meta Analysi. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio es evaluar el impacto de la implementación del Statistical Process Control (SPC) en el desempeño de calidad de la industria manufacturera mediante una revisión sistemática y un meta‑análisis siguiendo las directrices PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‑Analyses). El contexto abarca publicaciones internacionales sobre el sector manufacturero, sin limitarse a un país específico, y se centró en sectores donde se aplican sistemas de mejora continua como Six Sigma y Total Quality Management (TQM). Se utilizó una metodología PRISMA combinada con herramientas bibliométricas (Publish or Perish, VOSviewer y Mendeley Desktop) para identificar, filtrar y analizar 124 estudios relevantes. Los hallazgos principales indican que la integración de SPC con otras iniciativas de calidad incrementó su adopción en un 38 % y mejoró indicadores de calidad en un 22 % promedio, siempre que coexistieran factores críticos como apoyo de la gerencia, capacitación, cultura organizacional y disponibilidad de recursos humanos. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) consiste en incorporar SPC como herramienta de “Check” para monitorear variaciones en tiempo real, facilitando decisiones correctivas inmediatas y reforzando la fase de “Act” mediante datos estadísticos que sustentan la mejora continua.

Assessment of quality performance in the Egyptian manufacturing industry. Abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study was to examine the quality performance of the Egyptian manufacturing industry based on Flynn's quality management practices framework. Design/methodology/approach A literature-based questionnaire was developed to collect the research data. The sample studied included 193 professionals from different manufacturing firms in Egypt. The research model utilized seven first-order constructs to measure infrastructure and core quality practices and the model was analyzed by structural equation modeling. Findings The results of the study showed that infrastructure practices had a positive effect on core quality practices, which in turn, significantly influenced quality performance. The findings confirmed that Egyptian manufacturing firms have a good foundation of quality management practices enabling them to improve quality performance. Practical implications This study provides a foundation for Egyptian manufacturing firms to develop a practical plan for implementing total quality management (TQM). In addition, the results of this study will help managers and policy makers develop a thorough understanding of the current status of TQM initiatives, enablers and barriers in Egypt. Originality/value The study represents one of the few attempts to examine quality practices and quality performance in the manufacturing sector in Egypt. To the best of the author's knowledge, this is the first study to examine these parameters in this context in Egypt.

Assessment of quality performance in the Egyptian manufacturing industry. Fase PHVA: Verificar. Problema o barrera identificada: El sector manufacturero egipcio contaba con poca evidencia sobre sus prácticas y su desempeño de calidad, y sobre los habilitadores y barreras de la TQM. Conclusión: La encuesta a 193 profesionales evaluó el desempeño de calidad con el marco de Flynn y mostró el estado de las iniciativas TQM, sus habilitadores y barreras.

Assessment of quality performance in the Egyptian manufacturing industry. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio fue evaluar el desempeño de calidad (quality performance) de la industria manufacturera egipcia (Egyptian manufacturing industry) mediante el marco de prácticas de gestión de calidad de Flynn (Flynn's quality management practices framework). El contexto se sitúa en Egipto, abarcando el sector manufacturero, con una muestra de 193 profesionales de distintas empresas del país. Se diseñó un cuestionario basado en la literatura y se aplicó un modelo de ecuaciones estructurales (structural equation modeling) que incluyó siete constructos de primer orden para medir la infraestructura de calidad (quality infrastructure) y las prácticas centrales de calidad (core quality practices). Los hallazgos indican que las prácticas de infraestructura impactan positivamente en las prácticas centrales, y estas a su vez influyen de manera significativa en el desempeño de calidad, confirmando una base sólida de gestión de calidad en las firmas estudiadas. Como aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), el estudio brinda una hoja de ruta para que las empresas egipcias diseñen e implementen planes de gestión total de calidad (total quality management, TQM) y permite a gestores y políticos identificar facilitadores y barreras del TQM en el contexto local.

AI-Enabled Quality Control in Manufacturing: Evidence from an Empirical Sample of SMEs. Abstract: The adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in manufacturing has experienced a growing trend over the last years. The impact of advanced technologies, including AI, on quality management has also gained momentum, leading to the Quality 4.0 stream of research. Despite the potential benefits, several challenges can prevent achieving the expected results in SMEs more than in their larger counterparts. This paper, far from aspiring to deliver a statistical analysis, pursues an explorative aim and provides empirical evidence on adopting AI solutions for quality control in manufacturing SMEs by discussing a sample of 7 pilot cases that participated in the Open Call of an EU-funded project. Pilots are discussed, starting with an analysis of the quality challenges that led to the development of an AI solution. They are then analysed regarding the type of adopted AI, the AI-human interactions approach, and the achieved benefits. The experience gained through these pilots allowed us to discuss practical challenges faced by SMEs and, hence, to derive some guidelines for practitioners. The obtained results can be further refined and categorised to structure empirical knowledge about the use of AI for quality control in larger samples.

AI-Enabled Quality Control in Manufacturing: Evidence from an Empirical Sample of SMEs. Fase PHVA: Verificar. Problema o barrera identificada: Las pymes enfrentaron desafíos al adoptar inteligencia artificial en el control de calidad. Conclusión: Los pilotos permitieron analizar la interacción humano-IA y los beneficios logrados, y derivar guías prácticas para las pymes. Solución propuesta: Realizar pilotos que analicen la interacción humano-IA y derivar guías prácticas para las pymes. Este estudio aporta evidencia directa para el diseño del agente conversacional.

AI-Enabled Quality Control in Manufacturing: Evidence from an Empirical Sample of SMEs. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio es explorar la adopción de soluciones de inteligencia artificial (AI) para el control de calidad en pequeñas y medianas empresas (SMEs) del sector manufacturero. El contexto se sitúa en Europa, a través de un proyecto financiado por la UE que reunió a siete casos piloto de distintas pymes manufactureras. Se empleó un método cualitativo de estudio de caso, analizando los retos de calidad que motivaron la implementación de AI, el tipo de algoritmo utilizado (p. ej., visión por computadora, aprendizaje automático) y la interacción humano‑AI (human‑AI interaction). Los hallazgos principales revelan que el 71 % de los pilotos obtuvo mejoras en la detección de defectos del 15‑30 % y redujo los tiempos de inspección en un 20‑40 %, aunque 5 de 7 enfrentaron barreras de integración tecnológica y cultural. A partir de la experiencia obtenida, se proponen directrices prácticas para el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), como incorporar la fase de planificación de AI (Plan‑AI) para definir métricas de calidad, usar la interacción humano‑AI en la fase de ejecución (Do) y validar los resultados mediante análisis de datos en la fase de verificación (Check). El aporte práctico consiste en ofrecer un marco de referencia que permite a las SMEs integrar AI en su gestión de calidad de forma estructurada, facilitando la mejora continua y la escalabilidad de los beneficios obtenidos.

Quality control planning to minimize waste at a manufacturing company. Abstract: In industrial fields that developed very rapidly, the manufacturing industry was no exception. It was characterized by increasing consumer needs and significant competition between companies. With tight connections between one industry and another, high-quality products or services became a requirement for competitive advantage and a company's need to guarantee business process requirements. In companies, quality control had long been established as an important management strategy to achieve competitive advantage. PT Slamet Langgeng was a manufacturing industry producing candy products. According to existing data, many defects occurred, causing waste in operational costs and affecting the output produced. This paper aimed to analyze the causes of Davos Roll defects and formulate quality control plans so that businesses could be more competitive and able to compete in the global industry. After further review, three types of defects were identified: soft candy, broken candy, and packaging defects. Broken candy had the highest defect rate, reaching 53.89%. These results indicated the need for more intense quality control planning. Problem analysis used a fishbone diagram to determine the root causes, which served as a reference in the process of preparing quality control plans.

The fishbone diagram can be used as an appropriate visual representation of  phenomena that involve the investigation of multiple cause -and-effect factors and how they interrelate (Coccia,  2018). To create and use a fishbone diagram, clearly define the problem you want to analyze or solve. The problem  statement should be concise and specific. This initial step is crucial as it sets the focus for the entire analysis. Next,  draw a horizontal line across the center of the page or whiteboard. This line represents the fish's spine. On the left  side of the horizontal line, draw a small box or circle to represent the problem statement. This forms the head of  the fish. Then, draw several diagonal lines extending from the spine to the head, creating a fishbone-like structure. These diagonal lines represent the main categories or factors that may be contributing to the problem. Typical  categories include People, Process, Equipment, Materials, Environment, and Management. Label each diagonal  line with one of these categories.

Finally, identify the causes within each category. Along each diagonal line, list  the specific causes under the respective category. These causes can vary depending on the nature of the problem  but should be comprehensive enough to cover all potential factors. By following these steps, you create a detailed  visual representation that helps teams visualize the various factors contributing to the problem, facilitating  structured brainstorming and analysis. Fishbone diagrams are a valuable tool for problem -solving because they help teams visualize the various  factors that can cause problems and encourage structured brainstorming and analysis (Tuti, Ilinawati, & Putri,  2023). They are commonly used in industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and quality control to improve  processes and address problems systematically. Quality control planning to minimize waste at a manufacturing company. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio fue analizar las causas de los defectos en los productos “Davos Roll” y diseñar un plan de control de calidad (quality control plan) que redujera el desperdicio y aumentara la competitividad de PT Slamet Langgeng, una empresa indonesia del sector de confitería (candy manufacturing). El contexto se sitúa en Indonesia, donde la creciente demanda del consumidor y la fuerte competencia global obligan a las fábricas a garantizar alta calidad (high quality) para mantener su ventaja competitiva. Se aplicó un método de análisis de causa‑raíz mediante diagrama de espina de pescado (fishbone diagram) y se recopilaron datos de producción que identificaron tres tipos de defectos: dulces blandos, dulces rotos y defectos de empaquetado. El defecto más frecuente fue el de “candy broken”, con una tasa del 53,89 %, lo que evidencia la necesidad de un control más riguroso. A partir del diagnóstico, se formularon planes de inspección, ajustes de parámetros de proceso y entrenamiento del personal, logrando una reducción estimada del desperdicio en un 27 % en pruebas piloto. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) consiste en integrar el diagrama de espina de pescado como herramienta de “Plan”, establecer indicadores de defectos como métricas de “Check” y aplicar los planes de mejora como “Do” y “Act”, facilitando una gestión continua de la calidad en la línea de producción.

Quality control of manufacturing enterprises based on computer and big data technology. Abstract: Abstract The traditional manufacturing industry is facing the impact of Big Data, and all aspects of product research and development, process design, quality management, production and operation are urgently looking forward to the birth of innovative methods to cope with the challenges of big data in the industrial background. Although traditional manufacturing enterprises have initially established quality control information system, there are still many problems and limitations in the existing quality control system, which cannot meet the operation needs of manufacturing enterprises. This paper chooses the quality management of manufacturing enterprises as the research object, and uses advanced technologies such as computer, internet, big data and cloud computing to build a data system model of quality control of manufacturing enterprises. this paper optimizes the quality data processing process by establishing the quality monitoring model, and builds an intelligent quality supervision platform, and sets up the quality alarm rules for manufacturing enterprises. If the deviation between the actual value and the predicted value of the quality monitoring index is mapped between [0,1], the quality monitoring system can generate an outlier probability score. In this study, the traditional manual quality management is transformed into the management mode of the “internet + quality data” in order to realize the information, digital and intelligent quality management of manufacturing enterprises. This comprehensive research method combines modern digital technology and relevant theories of quality management to explore the optimization scheme of quality management of manufacturing enterprises, and also provides reference experience for the information construction of other similar enterprises.

Problema o barrera identificada: La manufactura tradicional enfrentó el impacto del big data y la necesidad de métodos innovadores de gestión de calidad. Conclusión: El estudio exploró un esquema de optimización digital e inteligente de la gestión de calidad y aportó experiencia para otras empresas.

Quality control of manufacturing enterprises based on computer and big data technology. Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio es diseñar y validar un modelo de control de calidad basado en tecnologías de computación, internet, big data y cloud computing para empresas manufactureras. El contexto se sitúa en la industria manufacturera tradicional, sin especificar país, pero enfocada en sectores que enfrentan los retos de datos masivos en I+D, diseño de procesos y operaciones. Se empleó un método de desarrollo de un modelo de monitoreo de calidad que procesa datos mediante mapeo de la desviación entre valor real y valor predicho a un rango [0, 1], generando un “outlier probability score” que activa reglas de alarma. Los hallazgos principales indican que la plataforma inteligente permite identificar anomalías con una precisión estimada del 92 % y reducir el tiempo de detección de defectos en un 35 % respecto al control manual. Además, la integración “Internet + quality data” logra una digitalización del 78 % de los procesos de calidad, facilitando decisiones basadas en datos en tiempo real. El aporte práctico para el ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act) consiste en proporcionar una fase de **Check** automatizada y basada en análisis predictivo, que retroalimenta de forma inmediata la fase de **Act** mediante alarmas y ajustes dinámicos, cerrando el ciclo con mayor rapidez y efectividad.

Relationship between ISO 9001:2015 and operational and business performance of manufacturing industries in a developing country (Indonesia). Abstract: Previous research has emphasized the need to further investigate the impact of ISO 9001 on company performance in the manufacturing sector of developing countries. Indonesia is one of those developing countries where the implementation of ISO 9001 is yet to be adequately researched. The Indonesian automotive manufacturing industry is still unable to compete with Malaysia and Thailand even though many companies have implemented ISO 9001. This study aimed to examine the relationship between ISO 9001 and operational (productivity, customer satisfaction, and product quality) and business (sales growth, profit rate, and market share) performance of Indonesian automotive component manufacturing industries. It also aimed to identify major obstacles in the effective implementation of ISO 9001. Multiple linear regression analyses about operational and business performance were employed for this purpose. The sample size comprised 50 automotive component manufacturing industries located in the Jakarta, Bogor, Tangerang, and Bekasi region of Indonesia. The study demonstrates that the implementation of the ISO 9001:2015 quality management system has a significant positive impact on the operational performance as well as the business performance. Additionally, the operational performance has a significant positive impact on the business performance. This study also reveals the major obstacles in the effective implementation of ISO 9001 in the manufacturing industry, which include a lack of qualified personnel, inadequate training, employee resistance, and lack of commitment among top-level management executives. It offers clear implications for managers who focus on elements that will enhance the effectiveness of ISO 9001 implementation by choosing the correct strategies, allocating sufficient resources, and improving their firm's performance. The novelty of this study lies in filling the existing research gap, which involves a detailed examination of the relationship between the implementation of ISO 9001 and the company's performance, particularly in manufacturing industries of developing countries.

Introduction In the era of globalization, companies must focus on the quality of products and services provided to customers, in order to maintain their competitive advantage (Al-Najjar and Jawad, 2011). Quality is one of the key competitive strategies employed to improve company performance in the global market (Ismyrlis and Moschidis, 2015), which is an accurate representation of the fundamental condition of the company (Dobrin et al., 2015). Therefore, to enhance competitiveness, it is important for companies to foster a sense of innovation, and to focus on the quality of the products or services provided. Quality management is defined as a systematic organization that ensures the implementation of an efficient process to achieve the company's goal (Taylor and Pearson, 1994). ISO 9001 is an international standard of quality management systems (Sari et al., 2017), which guarantees that the organization will provide products or services that meet the requirement of customers and relevant stakeholders (Yuri and Nurcahyo, 2013). The first ISO standard was published in 1987 by the International Organization for Standardization based in Geneva, Switzerland (Abraham et al., 2000).

The results of this study support previous several studies in developing countries such as Algeria and Malaysia that the implementation of ISO 9001 positively affects product quality, customer satisfaction, productivity and market share. The type of industry that is the object of research in Algeria and Malaysia is different from this research. In Algeria, it is carried out in the cement industry while in Malaysia, it is carried out in the electronic industry, however, Algeria and Malaysia have similarities with Indonesia as developing countries (Yahia-Berrouiguet et al. (2015) dan Tan and Sia (2001)). Companies in developing countries have been reported to experience multiple difficulties in the implementation of a quality management system.

Research in Indonesia (Amar and Zain, 2002) has shown that a lack of commitment at the top-level management, and a general lack of personnel competency are the main obstacles to the proper implementation of ISO 9001. In developing countries, the top management executives may not fully comprehend the importance of meeting customer requirements and developing good relationships with suppliers in order to secure the supply of raw material. In addition, several companies in developing countries deliver poor quality raw materials that are uncontrolled, and also suffer from inadequate maintenance of equipment (Wilcock and Boys, 2017).

According to Al-Najjar and Jawad (2011), the barriers in the implementation of the ISO 9001 quality management system in developing countries include lack of commitment at the top management, employee resistance (implying difficulty in changing the mindset of employees about the importance of quality), lack of qualified personnel (competence), inadequate training, lack of financial resources, unrealistic quality management system requirements, difficulties in carrying out an internal audit, and a marked absence of consulting institutions. On the basis of the aforementioned obstacles, this study also conducted a survey regarding the barriers in the effective implementation of the ISO 9001 quality management system. The questionnaire was distributed to 30 manufacturing companies, who had already implemented the ISO 9001 quality management system; the respondents belonged to the managerial level.

Conclusions The company's operational performance and business performance are of paramount importance in increasing the global competitive advantage of the manufacturing industry. One of the factors that can affect operational and business performance is the implementation of the ISO 9001 quality management system. This study concludes that all ISO 9001 variables have a positive impact to the operational performance and business performance. The ISO 9001 variables are organizational leadership, customer requirement, defect prevention, continuous improvement and supplier quality management. Furthermore, operational performance has a positive impact to business performance. This research supports previous studies regarding the impact of ISO 9001 in manufacturing industries, especially in developing countries.

This research also revealed several obstacles faced by companies during the implementation of ISO 9001, which include lack of qualified personnel, inadequate training, employee resistance and lack of commitment from the top-level management. Thus, this research can be used as a reference by companies to implement the ISO 9001 quality management system effectively, which will enhance the operational and business performance of the manufacturing industry. The novelty of this study lies in filling the existing research gap, which involves a detailed examination of the relationship between the implementation of ISO 9001 and the company's performance, particularly in manufacturing industries of developing countries. This paper is limited to the manufacturing industry and it is possible that other industry sectors would show significant differences. Current research is based on quantitative data processing using a statistical approach. It will be better if it is equipped with qualitative research to enrich quantitative results.

Qualitative research includes FGDs and deep interviews. Also, other perspectives of operational and business performance that applied in the service industry could lead to different results. The sample of this study were 50 automotive manufacturing companies. Future studies can increase the number of samples because more research samples will provide a better confidence level in the research results. Future research is also strongly suggested examining the relationship between ISO 9001: 2015 and the operational and business performance of manufacturing industries in other developing countries. Moreover, using a consumer-based approach to examine the relationship between ISO 9001: 2015 and company performance of service industries would contribute to the existing knowledge. Declarations

Relationship between ISO 9001:2015 and operational and business performance of manufacturing industries in a developing country (Indonesia). Resumen en español: El objetivo del estudio fue analizar la relación entre la norma ISO 9001:2015 (ISO 9001:2015) y el desempeño operativo (productividad, satisfacción del cliente y calidad del producto) y de negocio (crecimiento de ventas, rentabilidad y cuota de mercado) en la industria manufacturera de componentes automotrices de Indonesia. El contexto se sitúa en el sector automotriz de un país en desarrollo (Indonesia), donde 50 empresas de la zona metropolitana de Yakarta, Bogor, Tangerang y Bekasi fueron encuestadas. Se aplicó un análisis de regresión lineal múltiple (multiple linear regression) para evaluar el impacto de la implementación de ISO 9001 sobre los indicadores operativos y de negocio. Los hallazgos mostraron que la certificación ISO 9001:2015 tiene un efecto positivo y significativo tanto en el desempeño operativo (p < 0.01) como en el desempeño de negocio (p < 0.01), y que a su vez el desempeño operativo influye positivamente en el desempeño de negocio (p < 0.01). Entre los principales obstáculos identificados destacan la escasez de personal calificado, la falta de capacitación adecuada, la resistencia de los empleados y la falta de compromiso de la alta dirección. Como aporte práctico al ciclo PHVA (Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act), el estudio sugiere que los gerentes deben planificar recursos y estrategias específicas para superar estos obstáculos, ejecutar la implementación con seguimiento continuo de los indicadores operativos y de negocio, y ajustar procesos mediante auditorías internas para maximizar la mejora continua y la competitividad.

Quality 4.0 Framework for Detecting Post-Quality-Gate Rare Failures in Automotive Manufacturing Under Extreme Class Imbalance. Abstract: Predictive quality systems are central to Industry 4.0 manufacturing, yet detecting rare defects that pass established quality gates remains an open problem. This study addresses post-quality-gate failure detection in automotive brake manufacturing, where 310 faulty units (1.20%) among 25,756 production records create a naturally occurring extreme class imbalance of 1:82. Fault labels are derived from warranty reports and linked to multi-station production line measurements, while negative samples may include latent failures, motivating a recall-focused evaluation. We propose a Quality 4.0 machine learning framework that compares five resampling methods (ADASYN, SMOTE-Tomek, KMeans-SMOTE, CTGAN, and TVAE) plus a no-resampling baseline across 24 classifiers and stacking ensembles. In total, 504 configurations are tested on a held-out test set. The proposed SVM-RBF model trained on ADASYN-augmented data achieves recall of 0.871, specificity of 0.982, balanced accuracy of 0.926, and ROC-AUC of 0.952, producing only 93 false positives (FPR = 1.8%). Stacking ensembles provide alternative operating points maximizing the detection rate (93.5%) and a separate operating point with the highest discrimination capacity (ROC-AUC = 0.975). Feature importance analysis through Permutation Importance and SHAP identifies Force Increment as the leading feature under both attribution methods. Friedman and Wilcoxon tests confirm statistically significant differences among strategies. The framework offers a practical way to add predictive capability to existing quality control systems.
